boards.name: ICSE
boards.description: ICSE (Class 10) and ISC (Class 12) are conducted by the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE). Classes 6 to 9 and 11 are school-examined on the CISCE syllabus.

mathematics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum organises Class VI Mathematics into six themes (Number System, Ratio and Proportion, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Data Handling); the key-concept sub-headings of the Number System and Geometry themes are used here as separate chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Mathematics, Class VI

chapters.name: Numbers
chapters.summary: Place value, operations and word problems on large numbers up to 8 digits, estimation, and the Indian and International systems of numeration.

chapters.name: Natural Numbers and Whole Numbers
chapters.summary: Natural and whole numbers, their properties (commutative, associative, distributive, identities), the number line and patterns in operations.

chapters.name: Negative Numbers and Integers
chapters.summary: The need for negative numbers, integers on the number line, their ordering and comparison, and addition and subtraction of integers.

chapters.name: Sets
chapters.summary: The idea and representation of sets, finite, infinite and empty sets, and the cardinality of a set.

chapters.name: Fractions
chapters.summary: Types of fractions, equivalent fractions, comparison and operations on fractions, and decimal fractions with place value and conversion.

chapters.name: Playing with Numbers
chapters.summary: Simplification of brackets, multiples and factors, divisibility rules, prime and composite numbers, prime factorisation, and HCF and LCM.

chapters.name: Ratio and Proportion
chapters.summary: Ratio as comparison, proportion as equality of two ratios, the unitary method, the idea of percent, and problems on speed, time and distance.

chapters.name: Algebra
chapters.summary: Constants, variables and unknowns through patterns, algebraic terminology, framing and evaluating algebraic expressions, and an introduction to linear equations in one variable.

chapters.name: Basic Geometrical Ideas
chapters.summary: Lines, line segments, rays, open and closed figures, angles, and the parts of triangles, quadrilaterals and circles.

chapters.name: Understanding Elementary Shapes
chapters.summary: Measuring line segments and angles, types of angles and pairs of lines, classification of triangles and quadrilaterals, simple polygons, and 3-D shapes with their elements and nets.

chapters.name: Symmetry
chapters.summary: Reflection symmetry of 2-D objects, taking mirror images and identifying axes of symmetry.

chapters.name: Constructions
chapters.summary: Constructions with straight edge, protractor and compasses: line segments, perpendicular bisectors, angles of 60, 120, 30, 45 and 90 degrees, angle bisectors, perpendiculars and circles.

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: Perimeter of different shapes, area of rectangles and squares, and conversion of units of mass, time, money and capacity.

chapters.name: Data Handling
chapters.summary: Collecting and organising data with tally marks and tables, pictographs, bar graphs, and the mean and median of up to ten observations.

physics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VI Physics as six themes: Matter, Physical Quantities and Measurement, Force, Energy, Light and Magnetism.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Physics, Class VI

chapters.name: Matter
chapters.summary: The meaning of matter, the three states of matter, and the characteristics and distinguishing properties of solids, liquids and gases.

chapters.name: Physical Quantities and Measurement
chapters.summary: Measuring length, mass, time, temperature and the area of regular shapes, with their units and symbols.

chapters.name: Force
chapters.summary: Force as a push or pull, its effects on the motion, direction, shape and size of objects, and friction with its types, advantages and disadvantages.

chapters.name: Energy
chapters.summary: Simple machines and their types, mechanical advantage, the orders of levers, and numericals on the principle of levers.

chapters.name: Light
chapters.summary: Rectilinear propagation of light and its applications, the pinhole camera, and natural shadows and eclipses.

chapters.name: Magnetism
chapters.summary: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials, properties of magnets, magnetic fields including the Earth's, making magnets, electromagnets, and care, storage and demagnetisation of magnets.

chemistry.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VI Chemistry as five themes: Introduction to Chemistry; Elements, Compounds and Mixtures; Matter; Water; and Air and Atmosphere.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Chemistry, Class VI

chapters.name: Introduction to Chemistry
chapters.summary: The meaning and importance of chemistry, its historical development, notable chemists, and chemistry in food, cosmetics, clothing, medicines and industry.

chapters.name: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
chapters.summary: Elements and symbols of the first 20 elements, molecules of elements and compounds, mixtures, and separation by sieving, sedimentation, decantation, filtration, evaporation, magnetic separation and sublimation.

chapters.name: Matter
chapters.summary: Classification of matter into solids, liquids and gases, the arrangement of particles and intermolecular spaces, and the effect of heat on matter.

chapters.name: Water
chapters.summary: The importance and sources of water, water as a solvent with solute, solvent and solution, and water pollution and conservation.

chapters.name: Air and Atmosphere
chapters.summary: Air as a mixture of gases, its percentage composition, uses of its components, and the atmosphere as the layer of air around the earth.

biology.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VI Biology as five themes (Plant Life, The Cell, Human Body, Health and Hygiene, Adaptation); the sub-headings of Plant Life and Human Body are used here as separate chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Biology, Class VI

chapters.name: The Leaf
chapters.summary: External structure of a leaf, simple and compound leaves, venation, functions and modifications of leaves, insectivorous plants, and vegetative propagation by leaves.

chapters.name: The Flower
chapters.summary: The four whorls of a flower, pollination and its agents, fertilisation, formation and parts of fruits, and the parts, types and germination of seeds.

chapters.name: The Cell
chapters.summary: Plant and animal cells, the structure and functions of the cell wall, cell membrane, plastids, nucleus, vacuole and cytoplasm, and differences between plant and animal cells.

chapters.name: Digestive System
chapters.summary: Organs of the digestive system and their functions, and the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

chapters.name: Respiratory System
chapters.summary: Main parts of the respiratory system, respiration versus breathing, the mechanism of breathing, and common respiratory diseases.

chapters.name: Circulatory System
chapters.summary: The heart, blood and blood vessels, the process of circulation, components of blood, blood groups, blood pressure, heartbeat and pulse.

chapters.name: Health and Hygiene
chapters.summary: Communicable and non-communicable diseases, their modes of transmission and prevention, and ways of keeping surroundings clean and hygienic.

chapters.name: Adaptation
chapters.summary: Habitats and the adaptations of plants and animals to aquatic, desert, mountain and aerial habitats.

english.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out English for Class VI in four skill areas (Listening and Speaking, Reading, Writing, and Grammar and Vocabulary in Context), each with learning outcomes and suggested content.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - English
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 33-41 (Class VI English: Listening and Speaking pp. 33-35; Reading pp. 36-37; Writing pp. 38-39; Grammar and Vocabulary in Context pp. 40-41)

chapters.name: Listening and Speaking
chapters.summary: Listening to stories, poems, narratives and lectures for aural/written comprehension; comprehending issues raised in spoken texts (public address, televised interview, internet videos); group discussions, debates, speech, drama and presentations; analysing language in newspapers, television and advertising; adapting tone, stress, gestures and voice modulation; dictation of chunks of language. Recitation may be included in internal assessment.

chapters.name: Reading
chapters.summary: Reading literary and non-literary texts on themes such as self and family, neighbourhood, the nation's diversity and heritage (myths, legends, folktales), the world, adventure, sports and yoga, adolescence, science and technology, peace, travel, mass media, art, health and environmental concerns, for comprehension and inference; discussing rhyme, rhythm, metre, imagery, metaphor and simile in poems.

chapters.name: Writing
chapters.summary: Simple messages, invitations, notices, short paragraphs, letters and applications; short compositions based on pictures; simple narrative and descriptive pieces; creative writing (stories, poems, dialogues); organising sentences in sequence with linkers such as 'firstly', 'then' and 'finally'; the process approach of planning, revising, reviewing, editing and rewriting. Classes VI and VII write informal letters.

chapters.name: Grammar and Vocabulary in Context
chapters.summary: Pronouns in the proper case, reflexive pronouns and pronoun-antecedent agreement; subject-verb agreement with intervening phrases and clauses; transitive and intransitive verbs; tenses and inappropriate shifts in verb tense; vocabulary in context, affixes and roots; using dictionaries and reference materials; figures of speech in context.

history-civics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out History & Civics for Class VI as numbered History themes followed by Civics themes, each with learning outcomes, key concepts and suggested classroom processes.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - History & Civics
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 140-151 (Class VI History Themes 1-6 pp. 140-149; Civics Themes 1-2 pp. 149-151)

chapters.name: The River Valley Civilizations
chapters.summary: History Theme 1: why the earliest societies developed near rivers, and what the early river valley civilisations contributed to human heritage, studied from historical evidence.

chapters.name: The Vedic Civilization
chapters.summary: History Theme 2: India's past about 3500 years ago, and how the Vedas and the Epics give insight into it and into the origins of present-day society.

chapters.name: Mahavira and Buddha - Great Preachers
chapters.summary: History Theme 3: the teachings of Mahavira and Gautam Buddha, the similarities and differences between the two, and the importance of Ahimsa and tolerance.

chapters.name: Rise of Kingdoms and Republicans
chapters.summary: History Theme 4: how rulers emerged in the past and how ambitions to expand kingdoms led to wars and invasions.

chapters.name: The Mauryan Empire
chapters.summary: History Theme 5: the Mauryan Empire, with emphasis on Emperor Ashoka's turn from war and his welfare state, and Chanakya's ideas in the Arthashastra.

chapters.name: The Golden Age - Gupta Empire
chapters.summary: History Theme 6: advances in trade, economy, literature, astronomy, Ayurveda and mathematics under the Guptas, and why the period is called the Golden Age.

chapters.name: Rural Local Self Government
chapters.summary: Civics Theme 1: the main features and functions of the Panchayati Raj System and its three tiers, and other rural local bodies.

chapters.name: Urban Local Self Government
chapters.summary: Civics Theme 2: the composition and functions of Municipal Corporations and the civic duties of citizens.

geography.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out Geography for Class VI as numbered themes, starting with representing geographical features on maps and ending with a study of continents or of India.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - Geography

chapters.name: Representation of Geographical Features
chapters.summary: Theme 1: types of maps by scale, representing scale, symbols and directions on a map, and diagrams of geographical features.

chapters.name: Landforms
chapters.summary: Theme 2: the forces that form mountains, valleys, plateaus and plains, and where these landforms are found on the world map.

chapters.name: Water Bodies
chapters.summary: Theme 3: seas, rivers and lakes and where they are in the world, and water pollution as a link between local and global issues.

chapters.name: Agriculture
chapters.summary: Theme 4: farming practices around the world, the geographical factors behind crop growth, and the distribution of major crops.

chapters.name: Minerals
chapters.summary: Theme 5: minerals and ores, their distribution in the world, and the need to conserve them.

chapters.name: Study of Continents: North America and South America
chapters.summary: Theme 6: an overview of North America and South America, with a case study from each continent.

computer-studies.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum names this subject Computer Studies and sets it out for Class VI as numbered topics, each with learning outcomes and suggested content.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - Computer Studies
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 298 (core concepts chart) and pp. 299-306 (Class VI Topics 1-8)

chapters.name: Categories of Computers and Computer Languages
chapters.summary: Topic 1: classifying computers by generation, type, purpose, size, speed, processing power and price; machine, assembly and high-level languages; translators.

chapters.name: File Management - Organisation of Data
chapters.summary: Topic 2: file formats and common file operations (edit, view, copy, move, delete) and organising files by type, name, size and date.

chapters.name: Word Processor - Tabular Presentation
chapters.summary: Topic 3: inserting, drawing and modifying simple and complex tables in a word processor.

chapters.name: Word Processor - Mail Merge
chapters.summary: Topic 4: using mail merge to create personalised letters for bulk mailing, and address or mailing labels.

chapters.name: Presentation - Visual Effects
chapters.summary: Topic 5: making slide presentations more attractive and interactive with animation, sound and video.

chapters.name: Scratch Programming - Introduction to Game Creation
chapters.summary: Topic 6: working with the Looks, Control, Pen and Sound blocks of Scratch to create games.

chapters.name: HTML - An Introduction
chapters.summary: Topic 7: what a web page and HTML are, and designing and saving a simple web page with an HTML editor.

chapters.name: Internet - Online Surfing
chapters.summary: Topic 8: internet services such as e-mail, e-commerce, blogging, podcasting and Google Drive.

mathematics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum organises Class VII Mathematics into six themes (Number System, Ratio and Proportion, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Data Handling); the topics listed as key concepts within the themes are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Mathematics, Class VII

chapters.name: Integers
chapters.summary: Multiplication and division of integers, properties of operations on integers, and word problems involving integers.

chapters.name: Rational Numbers
chapters.summary: Introduction to rational numbers with representation on the number line, their decimal representation, and word problems on rational numbers.

chapters.name: Fractions and Decimals
chapters.summary: Fraction as an operator, reciprocal of a fraction, and multiplication and division of decimal fractions.

chapters.name: Exponents
chapters.summary: Exponents with natural numbers, the laws of exponents through patterns, and their use in simple daily-life problems.

chapters.name: Sets
chapters.summary: Revision of sets, equal, equivalent and universal sets, and the cardinal property of sets.

chapters.name: Ratio and Proportion
chapters.summary: Revision of ratio and proportion and consolidation of the unitary method with its general expression.

chapters.name: Percentage
chapters.summary: Percentage as a fraction with denominator 100 and conversion between fractions, decimals and percentages.

chapters.name: Profit and Loss
chapters.summary: Application of percentage to profit and loss in single transactions.

chapters.name: Simple Interest
chapters.summary: Application of percentage to simple interest for time periods in complete years.

chapters.name: Speed, Distance and Time
chapters.summary: Problems relating speed, distance and time.

chapters.name: Algebraic Expressions
chapters.summary: Algebraic terms such as constants, variables, coefficients and like and unlike terms, generating expressions, and addition and subtraction of expressions with integral coefficients.

chapters.name: Simple Linear Equations
chapters.summary: Simple linear equations in one variable in contextual problems with two operations.

chapters.name: Inequalities
chapters.summary: Inequalities and the solution of simple inequalities in one variable.

chapters.name: Understanding Shapes
chapters.summary: Pairs of angles, properties of parallel lines cut by a transversal, the angle sum and exterior angle properties of triangles, and verification of Pythagoras theorem.

chapters.name: Symmetry
chapters.summary: Recalling reflection symmetry and the idea of rotational symmetry of 2-D objects (90, 120 and 180 degrees).

chapters.name: Representing 3-D in 2-D
chapters.summary: Counting vertices, edges and faces, nets for cubes, cuboids, cylinders and cones, and mapping the surrounding space by visual estimation.

chapters.name: Congruence
chapters.summary: Congruence through superimposition, extended to triangles and circles, and the criteria of congruence.

chapters.name: Construction
chapters.summary: Constructing a line parallel to a given line from a point outside it and constructing simple triangles.

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: Revision of perimeter, the idea of circumference of a circle, and areas of squares, rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, circles, rings and combined figures.

chapters.name: Data Handling
chapters.summary: Collecting and organising data for testing a hypothesis, mean, median and mode of ungrouped data, and constructing and interpreting bar graphs.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: A feel of probability through experiments such as tossing coins and throwing dice, tabulating outcomes and the notion of randomness.

physics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VII Physics as seven themes: Physical Quantities and Measurement, Force and Pressure: Motion, Energy, Light Energy, Heat, Sound, and Electricity and Magnetism.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Physics, Class VII

chapters.name: Physical Quantities and Measurement
chapters.summary: Measurement of volume, estimating the area of irregular shapes, density of regular solids, and calculation of speed with simple numericals.

chapters.name: Force and Pressure: Motion
chapters.summary: Motion as change of position with time, translatory, circular, oscillatory and periodic motion, uniform and non-uniform motion with average speed, and mass versus weight.

chapters.name: Energy
chapters.summary: Energy as the capacity to do work, its units and forms, inter-conversion of energy and the law of conservation of energy.

chapters.name: Light Energy
chapters.summary: Reflection and its laws, images formed by a plane mirror, the speed of light, primary and secondary colours, and the colour of objects.

chapters.name: Heat
chapters.summary: Heat as energy and its units, temperature scales, effects of heat, conductors and insulators, and conduction, convection and radiation.

chapters.name: Sound
chapters.summary: Sources of sound, sound as a longitudinal wave, amplitude and frequency, the need for a medium, reflection and absorption of sound, and its relative speed in different media.

chapters.name: Electricity and Magnetism
chapters.summary: The law of magnetism, electromagnets and the electric bell, current as flow of charge, cells and batteries, circuit symbols, series and parallel circuits, and conductors and insulators.

chemistry.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VII Chemistry as seven themes: Matter and its Composition; Physical and Chemical Changes; Elements, Compounds and Mixtures; Atomic Structure; Language of Chemistry; Metals and Non-Metals; and Air and Atmosphere.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Chemistry, Class VII

chapters.name: Matter and its Composition
chapters.summary: The definition of matter as having mass and occupying space, and its composition from tiny particles.

chapters.name: Physical and Chemical Changes
chapters.summary: Physical and chemical changes, how to distinguish and classify them, and the changes involved in change of state and change of energy.

chapters.name: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
chapters.summary: Identifying elements and compounds, homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures, and separation by evaporation, distillation, separating funnel, sublimation, fractional distillation and paper chromatography.

chapters.name: Atomic Structure
chapters.summary: Atoms, molecules and radicals, atomicity, names and symbols of the first 20 elements, and valency.

chapters.name: Language of Chemistry
chapters.summary: Chemical reactions and the characteristics by which they are observed, and writing word equations.

chapters.name: Metals and Non-Metals
chapters.summary: General properties of metals and non-metals, rusting and its prevention, uses of common metals, and metalloids.

chapters.name: Air and Atmosphere
chapters.summary: Composition of air, oxygen and combustion, reactions of elements with oxygen, acid rain and its effects, air quality, and respiration, combustion and rusting compared.

biology.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VII Biology as five themes (Tissue, Kingdom Classification, Plant Life, Human Body, Health and Hygiene); the sub-headings of Plant Life and Human Body are used here as separate chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Biology, Class VII

chapters.name: Tissues
chapters.summary: Plant tissues (meristematic, and simple and complex permanent) and animal tissues (epithelial, connective, muscular and nerve) with their location and functions.

chapters.name: Kingdom Classification
chapters.summary: The need for classification and the characteristics of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia, including the major invertebrate phyla.

chapters.name: Photosynthesis
chapters.summary: The definition and basic process of photosynthesis, factors affecting it, its significance, and an experiment to demonstrate it.

chapters.name: Respiration in Plants
chapters.summary: Respiration as an energy-releasing process, aerobic and anaerobic respiration with word equations, and differences between respiration and photosynthesis.

chapters.name: Excretory System
chapters.summary: Excretory organs and products, the kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder and urethra, filtration by nephrons, and common urinary disorders.

chapters.name: Nervous System
chapters.summary: The brain (cerebrum, cerebellum, medulla oblongata), the spinal cord and nerves, with their location and functions.

chapters.name: Health and Hygiene
chapters.summary: Allergy and common allergens, their entry routes, symptoms, seasonal and perennial allergies, and precautions for allergy-prone people.

english.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out English for Class VII in four skill areas (Listening and Speaking, Reading, Writing, and Grammar and Vocabulary in Context), each with learning outcomes and suggested content.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - English
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 42-48 (Class VII English: Listening and Speaking pp. 42-43; Reading pp. 44-45; Writing pp. 46-47; Grammar and Vocabulary in Context p. 48)

chapters.name: Listening and Speaking
chapters.summary: Listening to texts from different genres and registers (story, poem, narrative, lecture, speech, dialogue) for aural/written comprehension; comprehending speeches, lectures, discourse, debates and discussions; group discussions; using graphics, images, music and visual displays in presentations; analysing language in newspapers, television, billboards and advertising; adapting speech to context.

chapters.name: Reading
chapters.summary: Literary and non-literary texts across genres and registers on themes such as family and pets, community, the nation's diversity and heritage, myths and folktales, India's neighbours and other countries, adventure, sports and yoga, adolescence (drugs, values, life skills), science and technology, peace, travel, mass media, art and health.

chapters.name: Writing
chapters.summary: Messages, invitations, short paragraphs, formal and informal letters and applications; simple narrative and descriptive pieces; creative writing (stories, poems); posters; organising sentences sequentially with linkers such as 'however' and 'therefore'; the process approach of planning, revising, reviewing, editing and rewriting.

chapters.name: Grammar and Vocabulary in Context
chapters.summary: Phrases and clauses in simple, compound and complex sentences; active and passive voice; synonyms, antonyms and analogy in context; figurative language (irony, pun, personification, alliteration, metaphor, simile, assonance, onomatopoeia); age-appropriate and domain-specific vocabulary.

history-civics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out History & Civics for Class VII as numbered History themes followed by Civics themes, each with learning outcomes, key concepts and suggested classroom processes.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - History & Civics
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 151-162 (Class VII History 'The Medieval World' Themes 1-6 pp. 151-160; Civics Themes 1-2 pp. 160-162)

chapters.name: Medieval Europe - Rise and Spread of Christianity
chapters.summary: History Theme 1: Europe's transition from the ancient Roman Empire to the medieval Byzantine Empire, and the rise and spread of Christianity.

chapters.name: Rise and Spread of Islam
chapters.summary: History Theme 2: the conditions and processes behind the emergence of Islam and its spread across continents, and its effect on politics, life and culture.

chapters.name: The Delhi Sultanate
chapters.summary: History Theme 3: the rule of the Delhi Sultanate - its capital, administration, achievements and socio-cultural developments.

chapters.name: The Vijayanagar and Bahamani Kingdoms
chapters.summary: History Theme 4: the rise of these two South Indian kingdoms after the decline of the Tughlaq Empire, and their art and architecture.

chapters.name: The Mughal Empire
chapters.summary: History Theme 5: why and how the Mughal Empire became the most important empire of later medieval India, and Mughal art and architecture.

chapters.name: Making of Composite Culture
chapters.summary: History Theme 6: the legacy of the Bhakti and Sufi movements since the eighth century and the teachings of Bhakti and Sufi saints.

chapters.name: The Constitution of India
chapters.summary: Civics Theme 1: the need for a Constitution and the main features of the Constitution of India as the supreme law of the land.

chapters.name: Directive Principles of State Policy
chapters.summary: Civics Theme 2: the principles that direct the State to create opportunities for the welfare of all citizens.

geography.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out Geography for Class VII as numbered themes, starting with representing geographical features on maps and ending with a study of continents or of India.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - Geography

chapters.name: Representation of Geographical Features
chapters.summary: Theme 1: reading topographical sheets through directions, colours and conventional symbols, and measuring distances with a scale.

chapters.name: Atmosphere
chapters.summary: Theme 2: the importance of the atmosphere and the gases in it, and global warming and its impact on people.

chapters.name: Weather and Climate
chapters.summary: Theme 3: the elements of weather, how weather differs from climate, and instruments for measuring rain, temperature and pressure.

chapters.name: Weathering and Soil Formation
chapters.summary: Theme 4: types of weathering and how weathering forms soil, soil profiles and soil conservation.

chapters.name: Industries
chapters.summary: Theme 5: the factors that decide where industries are located, how industries are classified by inputs, and industrial pollution and its prevention.

chapters.name: Energy and Power Resources
chapters.summary: Theme 6: renewable and non-renewable energy resources and conserving energy in daily life.

chapters.name: Study of Continents: Europe, Africa, Australia and Antarctica
chapters.summary: Theme 7: an introduction to Europe, Africa, Australia and Antarctica, with case studies.

computer-studies.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum names this subject Computer Studies and sets it out for Class VII as numbered topics, each with learning outcomes and suggested content.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - Computer Studies
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 298 (core concepts chart) and pp. 307-313 (Class VII Topics 1-7)

chapters.name: Computer - Hardware Components
chapters.summary: Topic 1: external and internal hardware (monitor, keyboard, CPU, motherboard, drives, sound and video cards) and how hardware and software work together.

chapters.name: Number System - An Introduction
chapters.summary: Topic 2: the decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal number systems and converting between them.

chapters.name: Computer Virus
chapters.summary: Topic 3: what computer viruses are, their types, symptoms and harm, and antivirus software and protection.

chapters.name: Ethics and Safety Measures in Computing
chapters.summary: Topic 4: computer ethics, unethical practices such as cyberbullying, phishing and software piracy, online safety measures, and digital footprints.

chapters.name: Spreadsheets - An Introduction
chapters.summary: Topic 5: the components of a spreadsheet, entering different types of data, and creating, saving and modifying a workbook.

chapters.name: Database and DBMS - An Introduction
chapters.summary: Topic 6: databases and Database Management Systems, creating a database and writing simple queries.

chapters.name: HTML - Advanced Features
chapters.summary: Topic 7: advanced HTML tags for lists, images, links, tables and forms.

mathematics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum organises Class VIII Mathematics into six themes (Number System, Ratio and Proportion, Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Data Handling); the key concepts listed under each theme are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Mathematics, Class VIII

chapters.name: Rational Numbers
chapters.summary: Properties of rational numbers in general form (closure, commutativity, associativity, identity and inverse), their representation on the number line, rational numbers between any two rational numbers, and word problems.

chapters.name: Exponents (Powers)
chapters.summary: Writing repeated multiplication and division using integers as exponents, and the laws of exponents with integral powers.

chapters.name: Squares and Square Roots
chapters.summary: Patterns in square numbers, and square roots by the factor and division methods for numbers of no more than 4 digits and no more than 2 decimal places, with estimation.

chapters.name: Cubes and Cube Roots
chapters.summary: Patterns in perfect cubes, and cube roots by the factor method for numbers of at most 3 digits.

chapters.name: Playing with Numbers
chapters.summary: Writing 2- and 3-digit numbers in generalised form (100a + 10b + c), puzzles with missing digits, and deducing the divisibility tests for 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10.

chapters.name: Sets
chapters.summary: Union and intersection of sets, disjoint sets and the complement of a set.

chapters.name: Percentage
chapters.summary: Slightly advanced problems applying percentages, built on ratio and proportion, to daily-life situations such as banking, taxation and loans.

chapters.name: Profit, Loss, Discount and Tax
chapters.summary: Problems on profit and loss including overhead expenses, discount and tax.

chapters.name: Simple and Compound Interest
chapters.summary: The difference between simple and compound interest (compounded yearly up to 3 years or half-yearly up to 3 steps), arriving at the compound interest formula through patterns and using it for simple problems.

chapters.name: Direct and Inverse Variation
chapters.summary: Simple and direct word problems on direct and inverse variation.

chapters.name: Time and Work
chapters.summary: Simple and direct word problems on time and work.

chapters.name: Algebraic Expressions
chapters.summary: Multiplication and division of algebraic expressions with integer coefficients, and the identities (a ± b)² = a² ± 2ab + b² and a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b), avoiding common errors such as 2 + x = 2x.

chapters.name: Factorisation
chapters.summary: Factorising simple algebraic expressions of the types a(x + y), (x ± y)², a² − b² and (x + a)(x + b) using identities.

chapters.name: Inequalities
chapters.summary: Properties of inequalities and their use to find solutions of inequalities in one variable.

chapters.name: Linear Equations in One Variable
chapters.summary: Solving linear equations in one variable in contextual word problems involving multiplication and division, with simple rational coefficients.

chapters.name: Understanding Shapes
chapters.summary: The angle-sum property of quadrilaterals and, by verification, the properties of parallelograms and of the diagonals of rectangles, rhombuses and squares.

chapters.name: Representing 3-D in 2-D
chapters.summary: Matching pictures with nested and joint 2-D and 3-D shapes, drawing 2-D representations and nets of 3-D objects, and counting vertices, edges and faces to verify Euler's relation for cubes, cuboids, tetrahedrons, prisms and pyramids.

chapters.name: Construction
chapters.summary: Constructing quadrilaterals with compasses and straight edge given four sides and one diagonal, three sides and two diagonals, three sides and two included angles, or two adjacent sides and three angles.

chapters.name: Symmetry
chapters.summary: The idea of reflection symmetry and symmetrical shapes, and finding lines of symmetry by paper folding.

chapters.name: Circle
chapters.summary: Parts of a circle: centre, radius, diameter, arc, chord, sector and segment.

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: Area of a trapezium, a polygon and a semicircle, total and curved surface areas of a cube, cuboid and cylinder, and the volume and capacity of cubes, cuboids and cylinders.

chapters.name: Data Handling
chapters.summary: Arranging ungrouped data into groups, constructing and interpreting bar graphs of grouped data, and simple pie charts.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Consolidating the notion of chance through repeated throws of coins and dice, aggregating outcomes over many trials, and relating chance to life events.

physics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VIII Physics as eight themes: Matter, Physical Quantities and Measurement, Force and Pressure, Energy, Light Energy, Heat Transfer, Sound, and Electricity.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Physics, Class VIII

chapters.name: Matter
chapters.summary: The three states of matter in terms of the movement and energy of particles, and changes of state (melting, boiling, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, deposition and freezing) explained by the kinetic theory.

chapters.name: Physical Quantities and Measurement
chapters.summary: Measuring the density of irregular solids and of liquids, comparing densities of solids, liquids and gases, floatation in terms of relative density, and simple numericals on density.

chapters.name: Force and Pressure
chapters.summary: The turning effect of a force and moment of force, pressure and its units with simple numericals, and pressure exerted by liquids and gases, including atmospheric pressure.

chapters.name: Energy
chapters.summary: Work and its unit, kinetic and gravitational potential energy with simple problems, energy transformation in daily life, and the distinction between energy and power.

chapters.name: Light Energy
chapters.summary: Refraction with examples, concave and convex spherical mirrors and their terms, ray diagrams and real and virtual images, and dispersion of white light by a prism.

chapters.name: Heat Transfer
chapters.summary: Boiling compared with evaporation, and linear, superficial and volume thermal expansion with the expansivity of solids, liquids and gases.

chapters.name: Sound
chapters.summary: Pitch and frequency in wind, membrane and string instruments, monotone, and loudness, amplitude and the decibel.

chapters.name: Electricity
chapters.summary: Household consumption of electricity, live, neutral and earth wires, fuses and circuit breakers, static electricity, conservation, conduction and induction of charge, the electroscope, lightning conductors and electrical safety.

chemistry.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VIII Chemistry as nine themes: Matter, Physical and Chemical Changes, Elements, Compounds and Mixtures, Atomic Structure, Language of Chemistry, Chemical Reactions, Hydrogen, Water, and Carbon and its Compounds.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Chemistry, Class VIII

chapters.name: Matter
chapters.summary: The main postulates of the kinetic theory of matter, change of state in terms of interparticle space, attraction and collision, and the law of conservation of mass.

chapters.name: Physical and Chemical Changes
chapters.summary: Activities on familiar changes in nature, and distinguishing and classifying physical and chemical changes.

chapters.name: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
chapters.summary: Classifying substances as elements, compounds and mixtures by their properties, and separating mixtures with the principle behind each technique.

chapters.name: Atomic Structure
chapters.summary: Electrons, protons and neutrons, atomic number and mass number, and the valency of elements and radicals in terms of the hydrogen atoms they combine with.

chapters.name: Language of Chemistry
chapters.summary: Symbols of elements, formulae of compounds from the valencies of elements and radicals, and writing and balancing chemical equations using the law of conservation of mass.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions
chapters.summary: Types of chemical reactions with examples, basic, acidic, amphoteric and neutral oxides, and the effect of heat on oxides of some metals.

chapters.name: Hydrogen
chapters.summary: Hydrogen from the electrolysis of water and in the laboratory from zinc and acid, its properties and uses, and oxidation and reduction as addition or removal of oxygen or hydrogen.

chapters.name: Water
chapters.summary: Water as a universal solvent, solutions, suspensions and colloids, saturated, unsaturated and supersaturated solutions, water of crystallisation, reactions of metals with cold water and steam, and hard and soft water and its softening.

chapters.name: Carbon and its Compounds
chapters.summary: Allotropy and the allotropes of carbon, properties of graphite and diamond, and the laboratory preparation, uses and reactions (with lime water and litmus) of carbon dioxide.

biology.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets Class VIII Biology as six themes: Transport of Food and Minerals in Plants, Reproduction in Plants and Animals, Ecosystems, Human Body (Endocrine, Circulatory and Nervous Systems), Health and Hygiene, and Food Production; the two halves of Theme 2 and the three systems of Theme 4 are used here as separate chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE (RDCD), Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), First Edition, November 2016: Biology, Class VIII

chapters.name: Transport of Food and Minerals in Plants
chapters.summary: Diffusion, osmosis and root pressure, macro- and micronutrients and their deficiency symptoms, and transpiration, its role in xylem transport and the factors affecting its rate.

chapters.name: Reproduction in Plants
chapters.summary: Vegetative propagation by cuttings, budding and other methods in plants such as rose, potato and Bryophyllum, and pollination by insects such as butterflies and honeybees.

chapters.name: Reproduction in Animals
chapters.summary: Sexual reproduction as the fertilisation of an egg cell by a sperm cell to produce offspring that may closely resemble the parents.

chapters.name: Ecosystems
chapters.summary: Biotic and abiotic components, producers, consumers and decomposers, food chains, food webs and pyramids of numbers, and symbiosis, parasitism and predation.

chapters.name: Human Body: Endocrine System and Adolescence
chapters.summary: Hormonal control alongside nervous control, endocrine and exocrine glands, the thyroid, adrenal, pituitary and pancreas, changes during adolescence and the management of stress.

chapters.name: Human Body: Circulatory System
chapters.summary: The heart and the circulatory system, lymph, and the functions of red and white blood cells.

chapters.name: Human Body: Nervous System
chapters.summary: The neuron, reflex action and the functions of the nervous system.

chapters.name: Health and Hygiene
chapters.summary: Communicable and vector-borne diseases with their causative agents and symptoms, personal hygiene, vaccination and immunisation, the harmful effects of tobacco, alcohol and drugs, and simple first aid.

chapters.name: Food Production
chapters.summary: Bacteria, mushrooms and yeast in the food industry, agriculture, horticulture, pisciculture, apiculture and sericulture, the green and white revolutions, food and cash crops, and animal husbandry.

english.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out English for Class VIII in four skill areas (Listening and Speaking, Reading, Writing, and Grammar and Vocabulary in Context), each with learning outcomes and suggested content.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - English
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 49-55 (Class VIII English: Listening and Speaking pp. 49-50; Reading pp. 51-52; Writing pp. 53-54; Grammar and Vocabulary in Context p. 55)

chapters.name: Listening and Speaking
chapters.summary: Listening to texts of different genres for aural/written comprehension; comprehending speeches, lectures, discourse, debates and discussions; group discussions; analysing language in media and advertising; adapting tone, stress, gestures, body language, voice modulation and word choice; collating ideas to keep discussions relevant; multimedia presentations on social messages such as drug abuse, values and life skills.

chapters.name: Reading
chapters.summary: Literary and non-literary texts across genres and registers on themes including family, community, the nation's diversity and heritage, myths and folktales, the world, adventure, sports and yoga, adolescence, science and technology, peace, travel, mass media, art and culture, and health and sanitation.

chapters.name: Writing
chapters.summary: Paragraphs of 250-300 words; formal and informal letters (formal letters are introduced in Class VIII); advertisements, diary and journal entries, notices, posters, articles, reports, personal narratives, anecdotes, stories, poems, features and dialogues; argumentative writing; writing across disciplines; using technology for research; the process approach to writing.

chapters.name: Grammar and Vocabulary in Context
chapters.summary: Phrases and clauses and their function in sentences; sentence analysis into main and subordinate clauses; transforming simple sentences into complex or compound sentences; using phrases, idioms and figures of speech in context.

history-civics.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out History & Civics for Class VIII as numbered History themes followed by Civics themes, each with learning outcomes, key concepts and suggested classroom processes.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - History & Civics
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 163-175 (Class VIII History Themes 1-8 pp. 163-172; Civics Themes 1-2 pp. 173-175)

chapters.name: A Period of Transition
chapters.summary: History Theme 1: change in the world brought about by the Renaissance (14th-18th centuries), the Industrial Revolution and imperialism.

chapters.name: The Growth of Nationalism
chapters.summary: History Theme 2: the demands for equality and liberty that led to the revolutions in America and France and the end of monarchy there.

chapters.name: India in the 18th Century
chapters.summary: History Theme 3: the decline of the Mughal Empire after Aurangzeb, the rise of independent regional kingdoms, and India's transition from the Mughal era to the British period.

chapters.name: Traders to Rulers
chapters.summary: History Theme 4: how the British gained political control over India, including the Battles of Plassey and Buxar and expansionist policies.

chapters.name: British Policies and Impacts
chapters.summary: History Theme 5: British educational, administrative and economic policies and their impact on native traders, peasants and artisans.

chapters.name: The Great Uprising of 1857
chapters.summary: History Theme 6: the causes and results of the First War of Independence of 1857 and the beginning of the National Movement.

chapters.name: Socio-Religious Reforms
chapters.summary: History Theme 7: 19th-century socio-religious reform movements led by educated Indians, and resistance to colonial ideas of superiority.

chapters.name: India's Struggle for Freedom
chapters.summary: History Theme 8: the rise of nationalism, the founding of the Indian National Congress, and Gandhi's Satyagraha and non-violence leading to Independence.

chapters.name: The Three Main Organs of the Indian Government: Legislature, Executive, Judiciary
chapters.summary: Civics Theme 1: the Union Legislature (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), the Union Executive (President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Ministers) and the Judiciary, and their functions.

chapters.name: United Nations
chapters.summary: Civics Theme 2: the formation of the United Nations in 1945 and the work of its organs and agencies for peace, security and human welfare.

geography.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum sets out Geography for Class VIII as numbered themes, starting with representing geographical features on maps and ending with a study of continents or of India.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - Geography

chapters.name: Representation of Geographical Features
chapters.summary: Theme 1: contours, reading toposheets through contours, symbols and colours, and drawing valleys, hills and plateaus as contours.

chapters.name: Population Dynamics
chapters.summary: Theme 2: causes of population growth, the terms birth rate, death rate, population density and migration, and the effects of fast population growth, studied through a case study.

chapters.name: Migration
chapters.summary: Theme 3: types of migration and their socio-economic impact, including brain drain from India.

chapters.name: Urbanisation
chapters.summary: Theme 4: the concept, causes and effects of urbanisation and how it relates to migration.

chapters.name: Natural and Man-made Disasters
chapters.summary: Theme 5: case studies of selected disasters, disaster management, and the Government's role in it.

chapters.name: Asia: The Largest Continent
chapters.summary: Theme 6: the physical features and natural environment of Asia, the largest and most populous continent.

chapters.name: India: Geographical Features
chapters.summary: Theme 7: a more detailed study of India's geography, building on Class VI.

chapters.name: India: Human Resources
chapters.summary: Theme 8: people as a resource for socio-economic development, and how a healthy, educated and skilled population is an asset to the country.

computer-studies.overview: The CISCE Upper Primary curriculum names this subject Computer Studies and sets it out for Class VIII as numbered topics, each with learning outcomes and suggested content.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE Curriculum for Upper Primary Classes (VI - VIII), RDCD, First Edition November 2016 - Computer Studies
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 298 (core concepts chart) and pp. 314-319 (Class VIII Topics 1-6)

chapters.name: Operating System (OS) and Graphical User Interface (GUI) - Role and Functions
chapters.summary: Topic 1: the operating system and its functions (booting, managing peripherals, memory and CPU), and character (CUI) versus graphical (GUI) interfaces.

chapters.name: Spreadsheet - Functions and Charts
chapters.summary: Topic 2: built-in spreadsheet functions and charts.

chapters.name: Algorithms and Flowcharts
chapters.summary: Topic 3: writing algorithms and drawing flowcharts, with their standard symbols, to solve problems step by step.

chapters.name: Program Coding
chapters.summary: Topic 4: writing, compiling and running programs in a programming language, covering literals, declarations, the assignment operator and basic constructs.

chapters.name: App Development
chapters.summary: Topic 5: what apps are, common apps and their uses, and building an app with free app-development software.

chapters.name: Networks
chapters.summary: Topic 6: computer networks and their components and topologies, network devices (modem, switch, hub, router), protocols (HTTP, FTP, TCP/IP, IMAP, SMTP), the Internet and cloud computing.

mathematics.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX Mathematics is one three-hour, 80-mark paper with 20 marks of internal assessment, in eight sections: Pure Arithmetic, Commercial Mathematics, Algebra, Geometry, Statistics, Mensuration, Trigonometry and Coordinate Geometry. The numbered sub-topics of Algebra and Geometry are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - Mathematics (51), CISCE RDCD, January 2026
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-7 (printed pp. 1-4: Class IX sections 1-8)

chapters.name: Rational and Irrational Numbers
chapters.summary: 1. Pure Arithmetic: rational and irrational numbers as real numbers, surds and rationalising the denominator, representation on the number line, and proofs of the irrationality of √2, √3 and √5.

chapters.name: Compound Interest
chapters.summary: 2. Commercial Mathematics: compound interest as repeated simple interest over 2 or 3 years and by formula, interest compounded half-yearly, the difference between CI and SI, and rate of growth and depreciation (equal instalments excluded).

chapters.name: Expansions
chapters.summary: 3. Algebra (i): recall and use of (a ± b)², (a ± b)³, (x ± a)(x ± b) and (a ± b ± c)².

chapters.name: Factorisation
chapters.summary: 3. Algebra (ii): factorising a² − b², a³ ± b³, and ax² + bx + c by splitting the middle term.

chapters.name: Simultaneous Linear Equations
chapters.summary: 3. Algebra (iii): solving simultaneous linear equations in two variables (numerical coefficients only) by elimination, substitution and cross-multiplication, and framing equations for simple problems.

chapters.name: Indices / Exponents
chapters.summary: 3. Algebra (iv): positive, fractional, negative and zero indices, and simplifying expressions with the laws of exponents.

chapters.name: Logarithms
chapters.summary: 3. Algebra (v): interchanging logarithmic and exponential forms, and the laws of logarithms and their use in expanding expressions.

chapters.name: Triangles (Congruency)
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (i)(a): congruency of triangles by SSS, SAS, AAS and RHS, illustrated with cut-outs, and simple applications.

chapters.name: Isosceles Triangles
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (i)(b): problems (proofs not required) on angles opposite equal sides and the converse, the greater angle opposite the greater side and the converse, the sum of two sides exceeding the third, and the perpendicular as the shortest line from an outside point.

chapters.name: Mid-Point Theorem and its Converse, Equal Intercept Theorem
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (i)(c): proof and simple applications of the mid-point theorem, its converse and the equal intercept theorem.

chapters.name: Pythagoras Theorem
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (i)(d): area-based proof and simple applications of Pythagoras theorem and its converse.

chapters.name: Rectilinear Figures
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (ii)(a): proof and use of theorems on parallelograms, with the rhombus, rectangle and square as special cases distinguished by their diagonals.

chapters.name: Constructions of Polygons
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (ii)(b): constructing quadrilaterals (including parallelograms and rhombuses) and a regular hexagon with ruler and compasses only.

chapters.name: Area Theorems on Parallelograms
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (ii)(c): parallelograms and triangles on the same base and between the same parallels, and triangles of equal area on the same base having equal altitudes.

chapters.name: Circle
chapters.summary: 4. Geometry (iii): chord properties (the perpendicular from the centre, equal chords equidistant from the centre, the circle through three non-collinear points) and arc and chord properties for equal angles at the centre.

chapters.name: Statistics
chapters.summary: 5. Statistics: raw, arrayed and grouped data, tally marks, discrete and continuous variables, mean and median of ungrouped data, class intervals and frequency tables, converting to continuous intervals, and frequency polygons.

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: 6. Mensuration: area and perimeter of triangles (including Heron's formula) and quadrilaterals, area and circumference of circles including inner and outer areas, and surface area and volume of cubes and cuboids.

chapters.name: Trigonometry
chapters.summary: 7. Trigonometry: the six trigonometric ratios, ratios of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°, simple 2-D problems with one right-angled triangle, and ratios of complementary angles.

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.summary: 8. Coordinate Geometry: dependent and independent variables, plotting ordered pairs in the Cartesian plane, solving simultaneous linear equations graphically, and the distance formula.

physics.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX Physics (Science Paper 1) is one two-hour, 80-mark paper with 20 marks of internally assessed practical work, in eight sections; the two numbered parts of Fluids and of Electricity and Magnetism are used here as separate chapters.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - Science (52): Physics, CISCE RDCD, January 2026
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-7 (printed pp. 1-4: Class IX sections 1-8)

chapters.name: Measurements and Experimentation
chapters.summary: 1: SI, fps and cgs units, least count and zero error of Vernier callipers and the screw gauge, and the simple pendulum with the l versus T² graph and T = 2π√(l/g).

chapters.name: Motion in One Dimension
chapters.summary: 2: scalar and vector quantities, distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration, distance-time and velocity-time graphs, motion under gravity, and graphical derivation of the equations of uniformly accelerated motion.

chapters.name: Laws of Motion
chapters.summary: 3: contact and non-contact forces, Newton's first law and inertia, the second law with linear momentum and F = ma, the third law and action-reaction pairs, and the universal law of gravitation, g, mass and weight.

chapters.name: Fluids: Pressure
chapters.summary: 4. Fluids (i): thrust and pressure, p = hρg and its consequences (dam bases, divers' suits), and transmission of pressure in liquids and Pascal's law with simple numericals (hydraulic machines excluded).

chapters.name: Buoyancy, Archimedes' Principle and Floatation
chapters.summary: 4. Fluids (ii): upthrust and its properties, Archimedes' principle for bodies denser and lighter than the liquid, relative density of solids and liquids, and floatation of ships, submarines, icebergs and balloons.

chapters.name: Heat and Energy
chapters.summary: 5: heat and temperature (1 cal = 4.186 J), anomalous expansion of water and Hope's experiment, global warming and the greenhouse effect, and energy degradation.

chapters.name: Light
chapters.summary: 6: laws of reflection, multiple images in parallel plane mirrors, and concave and convex mirrors with ray diagrams, f = R/2, the sign convention and mirror-formula numericals.

chapters.name: Sound
chapters.summary: 7: transverse and longitudinal waves, the need for a medium, V = fλ, factors affecting the speed of sound and its comparison with light, and infrasonic, sonic and ultrasonic frequencies and their applications.

chapters.name: Current Electricity
chapters.summary: 8. Electricity and Magnetism (i): free electrons and types of conductors, charge and its quantisation, current, potential difference V = W/q, resistance, circuit symbols, sources of direct current, and Ohm's law with simple numericals.

chapters.name: Magnetism
chapters.summary: 8. Electricity and Magnetism (ii): magnetism induced in magnetic materials, magnetic field lines and their properties, the earth's magnetic field and the compass, and neutral points with a bar magnet along the magnetic meridian.

chemistry.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX Chemistry (Science Paper 2) is one two-hour, 80-mark paper with 20 marks of internally assessed practical work, in eight sections, each used here as a chapter.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - Science (52): Chemistry, CISCE RDCD, January 2026
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-8 (printed pp. 1-5: Class IX sections 1-8)

chapters.name: The Language of Chemistry
chapters.summary: 1: symbols, valency, radicals and formulae of compounds, balancing equations by hit and trial, and relative atomic and molecular masses with percentage composition.

chapters.name: Chemical Changes and Reactions
chapters.summary: 2: direct combination, decomposition, displacement and double displacement reactions, and energy changes in exothermic and endothermic reactions.

chapters.name: Water
chapters.summary: 3: water as a universal solvent, solutions, colloids and suspensions, solubility curves, water of crystallisation, efflorescence, deliquescence and hygroscopy, drying and dehydrating agents, hard and soft water and the removal of hardness, and making water potable.

chapters.name: Atomic Structure and Chemical Bonding
chapters.summary: 4: constituents of the atom, Rutherford's gold foil experiment and Bohr's model, the 2n² and octet rules, isotopes, and electrovalent and covalent bonding with orbit structures.

chapters.name: The Periodic Table
chapters.summary: 5: Dobereiner's triads, Newlands' law of octaves, Mendeleev's periodic law, the modern periodic law and table (groups 1-18, periods 1-7), and the alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens and zero group.

chapters.name: Study of the First Element - Hydrogen
chapters.summary: 6: position of hydrogen in the periodic table, hydrogen from water, dilute acids and alkalis, its laboratory preparation and the Bosch process, and oxidation, reduction and redox reactions.

chapters.name: Study of Gas Laws
chapters.summary: 7: behaviour of gases explained by molecular motion, Boyle's and Charles's laws, absolute zero, the gas equation, Kelvin-Celsius conversion and STP.

chapters.name: Atmospheric and Environmental Chemistry
chapters.summary: 8: acid rain, global warming and greenhouse gases, ozone depletion, and water pollution including toxic heavy metals (Minamata disease), plastics, sewage and pesticides.

biology.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX Biology (Science Paper 3) is one two-hour, 80-mark paper with 20 marks of internally assessed practical work, in seven sections; their numbered sub-topics are used here as chapters. The last five chapters come from the earlier demo bank and have no counterpart in this syllabus.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - Science (52): Biology, CISCE RDCD, January 2026
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-6 (printed pp. 1-3: Class IX sections 1-7)

chapters.name: The Cell: A Unit of Life
chapters.summary: 1. Basic Biology (i): cell theory, plant and animal cell organelles and their functions, the cell wall and membrane, and differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic, and plant and animal, cells.

chapters.name: Tissues
chapters.summary: 1. Basic Biology (ii): types of plant and animal tissues, their location, structure and functions, and their roles in physiological processes.

chapters.name: The Flower
chapters.summary: 2. Flowering Plants (i): complete and incomplete flowers, essential and non-essential whorls of a bisexual flower and their functions, and the meaning of inflorescence and placentation.

chapters.name: Pollination and Fertilisation
chapters.summary: 2. Flowering Plants (ii)-(iii): self- and cross-pollination, agents of pollination and features of flowers pollinated by them, events from pollination to the zygote, double fertilisation and triple fusion, and fruit and seed.

chapters.name: Seeds: Structure and Germination
chapters.summary: 3. Plant Physiology (i): structure of the bean seed and maize grain, monocot and dicot seeds, hypogeal and epigeal germination, and conditions for germination.

chapters.name: Respiration in Plants
chapters.summary: 3. Plant Physiology (ii): an outline of respiration with glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, aerobic and anaerobic respiration with equations, and experiments on gaseous exchange and heat production.

chapters.name: Diversity in Animal Kingdom
chapters.summary: 4: Kingdom Animalia, from the non-chordates (Porifera to Echinodermata) to all five classes of chordates.

chapters.name: Economic Importance of Bacteria and Fungi
chapters.summary: 5: useful roles of bacteria in medicine, agriculture (the nitrogen cycle) and industry, harmful bacteria in food spoilage, disease and bio-weapons, and fungi in brewing, baking, cheese and mushroom cultivation.

chapters.name: Nutrition
chapters.summary: 6. Human Anatomy and Physiology (i): classes of food and their functions, vitamins and deficiency diseases, balanced diet, cellulose, kwashiorkor and marasmus, and the structure and types of teeth with the adult dental formula.

chapters.name: Digestive System
chapters.summary: 6. Human Anatomy and Physiology (i): organs and glands of the digestive system, enzymes, and the digestion, absorption and assimilation of food.

chapters.name: Skeleton - Movement and Locomotion
chapters.summary: 6. Human Anatomy and Physiology (ii): functions of the human skeleton, the axial and appendicular skeleton, and immovable, slightly movable and freely movable joints.

chapters.name: Structure and Functions of Skin
chapters.summary: 6. Human Anatomy and Physiology (iii): parts of the skin and their functions, its derivatives (sweat and sebaceous glands, hair, nails, mammary glands), and heat regulation by vasodilation and vasoconstriction.

chapters.name: Health and Hygiene: Diseases
chapters.summary: 7. Health and Hygiene (i)-(ii): communicable, non-communicable, endemic, epidemic, pandemic and sporadic diseases, transmission by air, water and vectors, and bacterial, viral, protozoan and helminthic diseases with their symptoms and control.

chapters.name: Aids to Health
chapters.summary: 7. Health and Hygiene (iii): vaccination, immunisation, antitoxins, serum, antiseptics, disinfectants and antibiotics, and the body's local defence system.

chapters.name: Health Organisations
chapters.summary: 7. Health and Hygiene (iv): the major activities of the Red Cross and WHO.

chapters.name: Introducing Biology
chapters.summary: Introduces the meaning and scope of biology, its main branches, and contributions of some important biologists.

chapters.name: Five Kingdom Classification
chapters.summary: Explains the need for classification, binomial nomenclature and the characteristics of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

chapters.name: The Respiratory System
chapters.summary: Describes the human respiratory organs, the mechanism of breathing and the exchange of gases in the alveoli.

chapters.name: Hygiene
chapters.summary: Covers personal and community hygiene, safe drinking water and sanitation.

chapters.name: Waste Generation and Management
chapters.summary: Covers sources and types of waste, their effects on health and environment, and methods of disposal and management.

english.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Paper 1 English Language (Classes IX and X) is a two-hour, 80-mark paper of five compulsory questions: composition, letter, notice and e-mail, unseen comprehension with summary, and grammar; a further 20 marks come from internally assessed listening and speaking.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - English (01), CISCE RDCD, January 2026
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 1-2: Paper 1 English Language, Questions 1-5); PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4: internal assessment of listening and speaking)

chapters.name: Composition
chapters.summary: Question 1: a composition of about 300-350 words, chosen from several subjects (some may be prompted by pictures), testing the ability to describe, narrate, report, explain, persuade or argue, and to present ideas coherently in the right style.

chapters.name: Letter Writing
chapters.summary: Question 2: a formal or friendly letter chosen from two subjects; the format (address, introduction, conclusion) and a tone and vocabulary suited to the context are assessed.

chapters.name: Notice and E-mail Writing
chapters.summary: Question 3: for a given situation, write the text of a notice following the directions given, and an e-mail with the same content.

chapters.name: Comprehension and Summary
chapters.summary: Question 4: an unseen prose passage of about 500 words, with a vocabulary question, short-answer questions testing explicit content and inference, and a summary that separates main ideas from supporting detail.

chapters.name: Functional Grammar
chapters.summary: Question 5: compulsory short-answer items on functional grammar, structure and usage, covering prepositions, conjunctions, verbs and sentence structure.

chapters.name: Listening and Speaking Skills
chapters.summary: Internal assessment (20 marks, three assessments in Class IX): listening to a passage of about 300 words read aloud, followed by an objective test; and a two-minute oral presentation followed by a discussion with the examiners.

history-civics.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX History & Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1) is a two-hour, 80-mark paper with an internally assessed project worth 20 marks, divided into Section A: Civics and Section B: History.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - History, Civics and Geography (50): History and Civics, CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-6 (printed pp. 1-3: Class IX, Section A Civics and Section B History, internal assessment)

chapters.name: Our Constitution
chapters.summary: Civics 1: definition of a constitution, and the dates of adoption and enforcement; features including single citizenship, universal adult franchise, Fundamental Rights and Duties, and Directive Principles; how Fundamental Rights differ from Directive Principles; the meaning of a welfare state.

chapters.name: Elections
chapters.summary: Civics 2: the meaning of elections; the composition and functions of the Election Commission of India; direct and indirect elections; general, mid-term and by-elections.

chapters.name: The State Legislatures
chapters.summary: Civics 3: the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council; unicameral and bicameral legislatures; term, composition, qualifications for membership, and powers and functions.

chapters.name: The Harappan Civilisation
chapters.summary: History 1: sources (Great Bath, Citadel, seals, bearded man, dancing girl, dockyard, granaries, script); urban planning, trade, art and craft, and decline.

chapters.name: The Vedic Period
chapters.summary: History 2: the four Vedas and the epics as sources; early Vedic social organisation and the assemblies (Sabha, Samiti, Vidhatha); women and the economy in the Early and Later Vedic periods; the four classes, the four Ashramas and education.

chapters.name: Jainism and Buddhism
chapters.summary: History 3: sources (Angas, Tripitakas, Jatakas); why both arose in the 6th century B.C.; Jain doctrines (Tri-ratnas, Karma, Moksha) and Buddhist doctrines (Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, Nirvana).

chapters.name: The Mauryan Empire
chapters.summary: History 4: sources (Arthashastra, Indika, Ashokan Edicts, Sanchi Stupa); the kings in chronological order; administration; Ashoka's Dhamma and its impact.

chapters.name: The Sangam Age
chapters.summary: History 5: sources (Tirukkural, megaliths); society and the position of women; the economy (agriculture and trade).

chapters.name: The Age of the Guptas
chapters.summary: History 6: sources (Fa-hien's account, the Allahabad Pillar Inscription); the kings and administration; contributions to education (Nalanda), science (Aryabhatta), medicine (Sushruta) and culture (Kalidasa, the Deogarh temple).

chapters.name: Medieval India: The Cholas
chapters.summary: History 7(a): sources (inscriptions, Brihadishwara Temple); the Chola kings in chronological order, their administration, and Chola art.

chapters.name: Medieval India: The Delhi Sultanate
chapters.summary: History 7(b): sources (inscriptions, Qutab Minar); the dynasties in order; Alauddin Khilji's market, military and revenue reforms and Deccan expedition; Muhammad bin Tughlaq's transfer of capital, token currency, Doab taxation and plans of conquest.

chapters.name: Medieval India: The Mughal Empire
chapters.summary: History 7(c): sources (Ain-i-Akbari, Taj Mahal, Jama Masjid, Red Fort); the kings in order; Babur's three battles; Akbar's Rajput policy, steps towards integration, reforms and the mansabdari system.

chapters.name: Medieval India: Composite Culture
chapters.summary: History 7(d): the factors behind a composite culture; the principles and impact of the Bhakti and Sufi movements; the impact of Christian missionaries.

chapters.name: The Modern Age in Europe: Renaissance
chapters.summary: History 8(a): the definition and causes of the Renaissance (fall of Constantinople, decline of feudalism, new trade routes, printing press); its impact on art, literature and science (Leonardo da Vinci, Shakespeare, Copernicus); its consequences.

chapters.name: The Modern Age in Europe: Reformation
chapters.summary: History 8(b): the meaning and causes of the Reformation, Martin Luther's contribution, and the Counter Reformation.

chapters.name: The Modern Age in Europe: Industrial Revolution
chapters.summary: History 8(c): the definition and causes of the Industrial Revolution; the meaning of capitalism and socialism and why each arose.

geography.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX Geography (H.C.G. Paper 2) is a two-hour, 80-mark paper on the Principles of Geography, ending with world map work, with 20 marks of internally assessed practical or project work.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - History, Civics and Geography (50): Geography, CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-7 (printed pp. 1-4: Class IX, Principles of Geography units 1-7, internal assessment)

chapters.name: Our World: Earth as a Planet
chapters.summary: Unit 1(a): the shape of the earth and the conditions that make it home to humankind.

chapters.name: Our World: Geographic Grid - Latitudes and Longitudes
chapters.summary: Unit 1(b): the main latitudes and their uses; longitudes, the Prime Meridian, local and standard time, time zones, GMT and the International Date Line; finding locations; calculating time; great circles.

chapters.name: Our World: Rotation and Revolution
chapters.summary: Unit 1(c): rotation and its effects (day and night, the Coriolis effect); revolution and the inclined axis, which cause changing lengths of day and night and the seasons, with equinoxes and solstices.

chapters.name: Structure of the Earth: Earth's Structure
chapters.summary: Unit 2(a): the core, mantle and crust - their meaning, extent and composition.

chapters.name: Structure of the Earth: Landforms of the Earth
chapters.summary: Unit 2(b): fold, residual and block mountains; intermont and volcanic plateaus; structural and depositional plains; examples from the world and India.

chapters.name: Structure of the Earth: Rocks
chapters.summary: Unit 2(c): how minerals differ from rocks; igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks and how they form; the rock cycle.

chapters.name: Structure of the Earth: Volcanoes
chapters.summary: Unit 2(d): active, dormant and extinct volcanoes; their constructive and destructive effects; the main volcanic zones of the world.

chapters.name: Structure of the Earth: Earthquakes
chapters.summary: Unit 2(e): the meaning, causes and measurement of earthquakes; their destructive and constructive effects; the earthquake zones of the world.

chapters.name: Structure of the Earth: Weathering and Denudation
chapters.summary: Unit 2(f): physical, chemical and biological weathering; agents of denudation; the work of rivers (V-shaped valley, waterfall, meander, delta) and of wind (deflation hollows, sand dunes).

chapters.name: Hydrosphere
chapters.summary: Unit 3: the meaning of hydrosphere; how tides form and their pattern; the circulation and effects of ocean currents (Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Drift, Labrador, Kuro Shio, Oya Shio).

chapters.name: Atmosphere: Composition and Structure
chapters.summary: Unit 4(a): the troposphere, stratosphere, ionosphere and exosphere; ozone and its depletion; global warming and its impact.

chapters.name: Atmosphere: Insolation
chapters.summary: Unit 4(b): insolation and terrestrial radiation; factors affecting temperature (latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, slope, winds, ocean currents).

chapters.name: Atmosphere: Atmospheric Pressure and Winds
chapters.summary: Unit 4(c): factors affecting pressure; the pressure belts; pressure gradient and Coriolis effect; permanent, periodic, local and variable winds (cyclones and anticyclones); jet streams.

chapters.name: Atmosphere: Humidity
chapters.summary: Unit 4(d): relative and absolute humidity; forms of condensation and precipitation; relief, convectional and cyclonic rainfall.

chapters.name: Pollution
chapters.summary: Unit 5: air, water, soil, radiation and noise pollution - their sources, their effects on the environment and health, and preventive measures.

chapters.name: Natural Regions of the World
chapters.summary: Unit 6: location, area, climate, natural vegetation and human adaptation in the Equatorial, Tropical grassland, Tropical desert, Tropical monsoon, Mediterranean, Temperate grassland, Taiga and Tundra regions.

chapters.name: Map Work
chapters.summary: Unit 7: locating, marking and naming on a world outline map the natural regions and the listed oceans, seas, gulfs, straits, rivers, mountains and plateaus.

computer-applications.overview: In the ICSE 2028 syllabus, Class IX Computer Applications is a two-hour, 100-mark theory paper on Java programming with an object-oriented approach, together with 100 marks of internal assessment made up of at least 15 programming assignments and a project on ethical computing.

syllabusSource.title: ICSE Examination Year 2028 - Computer Applications (86), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-6 (printed pp. 1-3: Class IX theory topics 1-11); PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4: internal assessment)

chapters.name: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming Concepts
chapters.summary: Topic 1: procedure-oriented versus object-oriented programming; the four OOP principles; open source, IDEs and tools (OpenJDK, BlueJ, NetBeans); Java applets and applications, the compilation process, bytecode and the JVM; Java's features.

chapters.name: Elementary Concept of Objects and Classes
chapters.summary: Topic 2: modelling entities as objects with state and behaviour; a class as a blueprint and object factory, and as a user-defined data type; computation as message passing between objects.

chapters.name: Identifiers and Literals
chapters.summary: Topic 3: the Java character set, ASCII and Unicode, escape sequences; tokens (keywords, identifiers, literals, punctuators, operators); primitive and non-primitive types; implicit and explicit type conversion.

chapters.name: Operators in Java
chapters.summary: Topic 4: unary, binary and ternary operators; arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment, increment/decrement and shorthand operators; precedence and associativity; the new and dot operators; print and println. Bitwise and shift operators are excluded.

chapters.name: Basic Structure of a Class in Java
chapters.summary: Topic 5: the standard structure of a Java class with a main method, including the version that imports java.util and uses the Scanner class for input.

chapters.name: Data Processing in Java
chapters.summary: Topic 6: input by initialisation, by parameters and through the Scanner class methods; introduction to packages; syntax, runtime and logical errors; single-line and multi-line comments.

chapters.name: Mathematical Library Methods
chapters.summary: Topic 7: the java.lang package and Math class methods (pow, sqrt, cbrt, ceil, floor, round, abs, max, min, random, rint, hypot and others) used in Java expressions.

chapters.name: Conditional Statements in Java
chapters.summary: Topic 8: if, if-else, if-else-if ladder, nested if, and switch-case with default, break and fall-through; menu-driven programs; System.exit(0).
