chapters.name: Looping / Iterative Statements in Java
chapters.summary: Topic 9: entry-controlled loops (for, while) and the exit-controlled do-while loop; converting between them; finite and infinite loops; break and continue.

chapters.name: Nested for Loops
chapters.summary: Topic 10: nested for loops with break and continue; square, rectangular and right-angled-triangle patterns of numbers and characters; series. Nested while and do-while are excluded.

chapters.name: Ethical Computing
chapters.summary: Topic 11: intellectual property rights (copyright, patent), privacy and data protection, spam, software piracy and cyber ethics, online safety, digital etiquette and responsible use of social media; done as a project and assessed internally.

history-civics.overview: ICSE History & Civics is Paper 1 of History, Civics and Geography (H.C.G., subject code 50). In Class X it is one 2-hour paper of 80 marks plus 20 marks of internal assessment (a project marked by internal and external examiners). Section A (Civics) covers the Union Legislature, the Union Executive and the Judiciary. Section B (History) covers the Indian National Movement (1857–1917), the Mass Phase of the National Movement (1915–1947) and the Contemporary World. The syllabus lists topics with lettered sub-topics, not chapters, so the sub-topics are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ICSE Examination Year 2027 syllabus: History, Civics and Geography (50), Paper 1 History & Civics, Class X

chapters.name: The Union Legislature
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 1. The federal setup, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, parliamentary procedures, the Speaker, and the powers and functions of Parliament.

chapters.name: The President
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 2 The Union Executive (a). Election, term, impeachment, and executive, legislative, financial, judicial, discretionary and emergency powers.

chapters.name: The Vice-President
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 2 The Union Executive (b). Qualifications, election, removal, term and powers.

chapters.name: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 2 The Union Executive (c). Appointment, functions, collective and individual responsibility, and the Council of Ministers versus the Cabinet.

chapters.name: The Supreme Court
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 3 The Judiciary (a). Composition, appointment, independence, jurisdiction, judicial review and writs.

chapters.name: The High Courts
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 3 The Judiciary (b). Composition, appointment, jurisdiction and functions.

chapters.name: Subordinate Courts
chapters.summary: Civics (Section A), Topic 3 The Judiciary (c). District Judge's Court versus Sessions Court, and Lok Adalats.

chapters.name: The First War of Independence, 1857
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 1 The Indian National Movement (1857–1917) (a). Causes and consequences only.

chapters.name: Factors Leading to the Growth of Nationalism
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 1 (b). Economic exploitation, colonial policies, reform movements, the Press, and the foundation of the Indian National Congress.

chapters.name: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885–1907)
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 1 (c). Objectives and methods of the Early Nationalists.

chapters.name: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905–1916)
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 1 (c). Partition of Bengal, the Surat Split, the Assertive Nationalists, the Muslim League and the Lucknow Pact.

chapters.name: Mahatma Gandhi: Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience and Quit India Movements
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 2 Mass Phase of the National Movement (1915–1947) (a).

chapters.name: Forward Bloc and the INA
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 2 (b). Objectives of the Forward Bloc, and the INA and the contribution of Subhas Chandra Bose.

chapters.name: Independence and Partition of India
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 2 (c). The Cabinet Mission Plan, the Mountbatten Plan and the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

chapters.name: The First World War
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 3 The Contemporary World (a). Causes and results, including the Treaty of Versailles and the League of Nations.

chapters.name: Rise of Dictatorships
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 3 (b). The rise of Fascism in Italy and Nazism in Germany.

chapters.name: The Second World War
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 3 (c). Causes and consequences, including the formation of the UN and the Cold War (meaning only).

chapters.name: The United Nations
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 3 (d). Objectives, principal organs and major agencies, and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (meaning only).

chapters.name: Non-Aligned Movement
chapters.summary: History (Section B), Topic 3 (e). Meaning, objectives, Panchsheel, and the role of Jawaharlal Nehru.

geography.overview: ICSE Geography is Paper 2 of History, Civics and Geography (H.C.G., subject code 50). In Class X it is one 2-hour paper of 80 marks plus 20 marks of internal assessment (project work). Part I (Map Work) covers interpretation of topographical maps and the map of India. Part II (Geography of India) covers climate, soil, natural vegetation, water, minerals and energy, agriculture, manufacturing industries, transport and waste management.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ICSE Examination Year 2027 syllabus: History, Civics and Geography (50), Paper 2 Geography, Class X

chapters.name: Interpretation of Topographical Maps
chapters.summary: Part I: Map Work, Topic 1. Grid references, contours, conventional symbols, scale, directions, drainage and settlement patterns on Survey of India maps.

chapters.name: Map of India
chapters.summary: Part I: Map Work, Topic 2. Locating, marking and naming physical features, rivers, winds, minerals, soils, cities and population distribution on an outline map of India.

chapters.name: Climate
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 3. Factors affecting India's climate, the monsoon mechanism and seasons.

chapters.name: Soil Resources
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 4. Types of soil, soil erosion and soil conservation.

chapters.name: Natural Vegetation
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 5. Importance of forests, types of vegetation and forest conservation.

chapters.name: Water Resources
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 6. Sources, conservation, rainwater harvesting and methods of irrigation.

chapters.name: Mineral and Energy Resources
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 7. Iron ore, manganese, copper and bauxite, and conventional and non-conventional energy sources.

chapters.name: Agriculture
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 8. Indian agriculture, the Green Revolution, types of farming, cropping seasons and major crops.

chapters.name: Manufacturing Industries
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 9. Classification, agro-based (sugar, textiles) and mineral-based (iron and steel, petrochemicals, electronics) industries.

chapters.name: Transport
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 10. Roadways, railways, airways and waterways: advantages and disadvantages.

chapters.name: Waste Management
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 11. Impact of waste accumulation, safe disposal methods, and reduce, reuse and recycle.

mathematics.overview: ISC Class XI Mathematics (860) has a 3-hour, 80-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 20-mark project (Paper II). The theory has five units: Sets and Functions (18 marks), Algebra (26), Coordinate Geometry (20), Calculus (8) and Statistics & Probability (8). Their numbered sub-units are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2028 syllabus: Mathematics (860), Class XI

chapters.name: Sets
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Sets and Functions (i). Representation and types of sets, subsets and intervals, power set, universal set, Venn diagrams, and union, intersection, difference and complement.

chapters.name: Relations and Functions
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Sets and Functions (ii). Ordered pairs, Cartesian products, relations, functions as mappings, standard real-valued functions and their graphs, and algebra of functions.

chapters.name: Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Sets and Functions (iii). Radian and degree measure, trigonometric functions via the unit circle, their signs, domains, ranges and graphs, and compound, multiple-angle and sum-product identities.

chapters.name: Complex Numbers
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Algebra (i). Algebraic properties, the Argand plane and polar form, conjugate, modulus and argument, square roots of complex numbers, and cube roots of unity.

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Algebra (ii). Solution and nature of roots, forming equations from given roots, quadratic functions and their graphs, and linear and quadratic inequalities.

chapters.name: Permutations and Combinations
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Algebra (iii). The fundamental principle of counting, factorial notation, nPr and nCr, restricted and circular permutations, and mixed problems.

chapters.name: Binomial Theorem
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Algebra (iv). Statement and proof for positive integral indices, Pascal's triangle, binomial coefficients, and general and middle terms.

chapters.name: Sequence and Series
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Algebra (v). Arithmetic and geometric progressions, arithmetic and geometric means and their relation, infinite G.P., and the special sums of n, n squared and n cubed.

chapters.name: Straight Lines
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Coordinate Geometry (i). Section formula and area of a triangle, slope and angle between lines, forms of the equation of a line, distance of a point from a line, families of lines, and locus.

chapters.name: Circles
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Coordinate Geometry (ii). Standard, diameter, general and parametric forms of the equation of a circle, intercepts on the axes, and relative position of two circles.

chapters.name: Conic Sections
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Coordinate Geometry (iii). Conics as sections of a cone, focus, directrix and eccentricity, and the standard equations and properties of the parabola, ellipse and hyperbola.

chapters.name: Introduction to Three-dimensional Geometry
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Coordinate Geometry (iv). Coordinate axes and planes in three dimensions, coordinates of a point, the distance formula and the section formula.

chapters.name: Limits and Derivatives
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Calculus (i). Limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions, the derivative as rate of change and slope, first principles, and derivatives of sums, products and quotients.

chapters.name: Statistics
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Statistics and Probability (i). Range, mean deviation about the mean, variance and standard deviation of ungrouped and grouped data, and combined mean and standard deviation.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Statistics and Probability (ii). Random experiments, sample spaces, types of events, axiomatic probability, and the probability of 'not', 'and' and 'or' events.

physics.overview: ISC Class XI Physics has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory has ten units, with marks given for groups of units (units 1-3: 23 marks, 4-6: 17, 7-9: 20, 10: 10). Their numbered sub-units are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2028 syllabus: Physics, Class XI
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-12 (the PDF text layer carries no printed page numbers)

chapters.name: Units and Measurements
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Physical World and Measurement. Systems of units and SI base units, errors in measurement, significant figures, and dimensions and dimensional analysis.

chapters.name: Motion in a Straight Line
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Kinematics (i). Frame of reference, speed, velocity and acceleration, motion graphs, equations of uniformly accelerated motion, and elementary differentiation and integration.

chapters.name: Motion in a Plane
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Kinematics (ii). Scalars and vectors, vector addition, resolution and products, projectile motion and uniform circular motion.

chapters.name: Laws of Motion
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Laws of Motion. Newton's laws, impulse, conservation of linear momentum, equilibrium of concurrent forces, friction, and dynamics of uniform circular motion.

chapters.name: Work, Energy and Power
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Work, Energy and Power. Work by constant and variable forces, kinetic and potential energy, the work-energy theorem, power, conservation of mechanical energy, and collisions.

chapters.name: Motion of System of Particles and Rigid Body
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Motion of System of Particles and Rigid Body. Centre of mass, torque, angular momentum and its conservation, rotational equations of motion, and moment of inertia with the parallel and perpendicular axes theorems.

chapters.name: Gravitation
chapters.summary: Unit 6: Gravitation. Kepler's laws, the universal law of gravitation, variation of g, gravitational potential and potential energy, escape and orbital velocity, and geostationary satellites.

chapters.name: Mechanical Properties of Solids
chapters.summary: Unit 7: Properties of Bulk Matter (i). Elasticity, stress-strain relationship, Hooke's law, Young's, bulk and shear moduli, Poisson's ratio and elastic energy.

chapters.name: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
chapters.summary: Unit 7: Properties of Bulk Matter (ii). Fluid pressure and Pascal's law, viscosity and Stokes' law, streamline flow and Bernoulli's theorem, and surface tension and capillary rise.

chapters.name: Thermal Properties of Matter
chapters.summary: Unit 8: Heat and Thermodynamics (i). Thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, calorimetry and latent heat, heat transfer, black-body radiation, Wien's and Stefan's laws, and Newton's law of cooling.

chapters.name: Thermodynamics
chapters.summary: Unit 8: Heat and Thermodynamics (ii). Thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law, heat, work and internal energy, the first law, isothermal and adiabatic processes, and the second law.

chapters.name: Behaviour of Perfect Gases and Kinetic Theory of Gases
chapters.summary: Unit 9: Behaviour of Perfect Gases and Kinetic Theory of Gases. Equation of state of a perfect gas, kinetic theory and pressure, kinetic interpretation of temperature, rms speed, degrees of freedom, equipartition of energy, and mean free path.

chapters.name: Oscillations
chapters.summary: Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves (i). Periodic motion, simple harmonic motion and its energy, oscillations of a spring, and the simple pendulum.

chapters.name: Waves
chapters.summary: Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves (ii). Transverse and longitudinal waves, wave speed, progressive waves, superposition and reflection, standing waves in strings and organ pipes, harmonics, and beats.

chemistry.overview: ISC Class XI Chemistry has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory has nine units, with marks given by branch: Physical Chemistry 41, Inorganic Chemistry 6 and Organic Chemistry 23.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2028 syllabus: Chemistry, Class XI

chapters.name: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
chapters.summary: Unit 1. Laws of chemical combination, Dalton's atomic theory, atomic and molecular masses, the mole concept, empirical and molecular formulae, chemical equivalents, and stoichiometry.

chapters.name: Structure of Atom
chapters.summary: Unit 2. Fundamental particles, the Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr models, dual nature and the uncertainty principle, quantum numbers, orbitals, and electronic configuration.

chapters.name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
chapters.summary: Unit 3. Mendeleev's and the Modern Periodic Law, the long form of the periodic table, and periodic trends in atomic and ionic radii, ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy and electronegativity.

chapters.name: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
chapters.summary: Unit 4. Ionic and covalent bonds, bond parameters, Lewis structures, Fajan's rules, VSEPR theory, hybridisation, molecular orbital theory, resonance and hydrogen bonding.

chapters.name: Chemical Thermodynamics
chapters.summary: Unit 5. Systems and state functions, the first law with internal energy and enthalpy, the second law with entropy and spontaneity, and the third law.

chapters.name: Equilibrium
chapters.summary: Unit 6. Chemical equilibrium, the law of mass action and Le Chatelier's principle, and ionic equilibrium including pH, buffers, hydrolysis of salts and solubility product.

chapters.name: Redox Reactions
chapters.summary: Unit 7. Oxidation and reduction, oxidation number, and balancing redox reactions by the oxidation number and ion-electron methods.

chapters.name: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
chapters.summary: Unit 8. Classification, IUPAC nomenclature and isomerism of organic compounds, purification and analysis, electronic displacement effects, bond fission, and types of organic reactions.

chapters.name: Hydrocarbons
chapters.summary: Unit 9. Alkanes, alkenes and alkynes (nomenclature, preparation, properties) and aromatic hydrocarbons, with benzene and electrophilic substitution.

biology.overview: ISC Class XI Biology has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory has five units: Diversity of Living Organisms (9 marks), Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants (11), Cell: Structure and Function (15), Plant Physiology (17) and Human Physiology (18). Their numbered sub-units are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2028 syllabus: Biology, Class XI

chapters.name: The Living World
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Diversity of Living Organisms (i). The need for classification, taxonomy and systematics, the concept of species, taxonomic hierarchy, and binomial nomenclature.

chapters.name: Biological Classification
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Diversity of Living Organisms (ii). Three domains of life, five-kingdom classification of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia, and lichens, viruses, viroids and prions.

chapters.name: Plant Kingdom
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Diversity of Living Organisms (iii). Characteristics and examples of algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms.

chapters.name: Animal Kingdom
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Diversity of Living Organisms (iv). Levels of organisation, body plans, symmetry, germ layers and coelom as the basis of animal classification.

chapters.name: Morphology of Flowering Plants
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants (i). Morphology and modifications of root, stem and leaf, the structure of a typical flower, and types of inflorescence.

chapters.name: Anatomy of Flowering Plants
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants (ii). Meristematic and permanent plant tissues, tissue systems, and the internal structure of plant organs.

chapters.name: Structural Organisation in Animals: Frog
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants (iii). A brief account of the morphology, anatomy and organ systems of the frog.

chapters.name: Cell: The Unit of Life
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Cell: Structure and Function (i). Cell theory, prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, the cell envelope, membrane and wall, and the ultrastructure and functions of cell organelles.

chapters.name: Biomolecules
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Cell: Structure and Function (ii). Carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, enzymes and secondary metabolites.

chapters.name: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Cell: Structure and Function (iii). Stages of the cell cycle, and mitosis and meiosis with their significance.

chapters.name: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Plant Physiology (i). Site and pigments of photosynthesis, photochemical and biosynthetic phases, photophosphorylation, the chemiosmotic hypothesis, photorespiration, and C3 and C4 pathways.

chapters.name: Respiration in Plants
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Plant Physiology (ii). Glycolysis, fermentation, the TCA cycle and electron transport system, ATP yield, amphibolic pathways and respiratory quotient.

chapters.name: Plant Growth and Development
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Plant Physiology (iii). Seed germination, phases and rate of plant growth, differentiation, and the growth regulators auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, ethylene and ABA.

chapters.name: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Human Physiology (i). The human respiratory system, the mechanism of breathing, exchange and transport of gases, regulation of breathing, respiratory volumes and disorders.

chapters.name: Body Fluids and Circulation
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Human Physiology (ii). Blood, blood groups and coagulation, lymph, the human heart and blood vessels, the cardiac cycle, ECG, double circulation, and circulatory disorders.

chapters.name: Excretory Products and their Elimination
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Human Physiology (iii). Modes of excretion, the human excretory system, urine formation, osmoregulation, regulation of kidney function, and disorders.

chapters.name: Locomotion and Movement
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Human Physiology (iv). Types of movement, skeletal muscle and muscle contraction, the skeletal system, and joints and their disorders.

chapters.name: Neural Control and Coordination
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Human Physiology (v). Neurons and nerves, the central, peripheral and visceral nervous systems, and the generation and conduction of nerve impulses.

chapters.name: Chemical Co-ordination and Integration
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Human Physiology (vi). The human endocrine glands, the mechanism of hormone action, and disorders due to hypo- and hyperactivity of hormones.

english.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, English Language for Class XI is an 80-mark, three-hour theory paper of four compulsory questions (composition, directed and proposal writing, grammar, and comprehension with summary), plus 20 marks of project work assessing listening and speaking.

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - English (801): English Language, CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 1-2: Paper I Theory, Questions One-Four); PDF p. 6 (printed p. 3: Project Work for Class XI)

chapters.name: Composition
chapters.summary: Question One: one composition of 400-450 words chosen from six topics (narrative, descriptive, reflective, argumentative/persuasive, expository, or an original short story), marked on quality of language and organisation.

chapters.name: Directed Writing
chapters.summary: Question Two (a): 250-300 words based on given information and points - a feature article, book review, blog, newspaper report or statement of purpose - with the correct format.

chapters.name: Proposal Writing
chapters.summary: Question Two (b): a proposal for a given situation, in the format prescribed by CISCE, with an introduction or heading, objectives, a list of measures and a concluding statement.

chapters.name: Grammar
chapters.summary: Question Three: compulsory short-answer items testing functional grammar and structure - transformation of sentences, phrasal verbs, and verbs and tenses.

chapters.name: Comprehension and Summary
chapters.summary: Question Four: a passage of about 700 words with questions on analysis, vocabulary, content and inference, and a summary written in grid form within a word limit.

chapters.name: Listening and Speaking Skills (Project Work)
chapters.summary: Paper II for Class XI (20 marks, assessed internally): a listening test on an unseen 500-word passage read aloud twice, and a three-minute individual presentation followed by a discussion.

accountancy.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Accountancy is an 80-mark, three-hour theory paper of ten units, from Introduction to Accounting to the Computerised Accounting System, plus 20 marks of project work (two projects).

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Accountancy (858), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1: unit weightage table); PDF pp. 5-8 (printed pp. 2-5: Paper I units 1-10); PDF pp. 9-10 (project work)

chapters.name: Introduction to Accounting
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (2 marks): a brief history of accounting; basic terms (transactions, vouchers, capital, assets, liabilities, stock, revenue, drawings); book-keeping, accounting and accountancy; the accounting cycle; stakeholders; financial, cost and management accounting.

chapters.name: Accounting Concepts
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (4 marks): GAAP concepts (going concern, entity, money measurement, accrual, dual aspect, matching, prudence and others); cash and accrual bases; Accounting Standards; a brief introduction to IFRS.

chapters.name: Journal, Ledger and Trial Balance
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (12 marks): the accounting equation; double entry and rules of journalising; the journal, ledger posting and balancing; subsidiary books (cash books, petty cash book, day books, journal proper); the Trial Balance. Transactions with GST are excluded.

chapters.name: Bank Reconciliation Statement
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (10 marks): the meaning of and need for a BRS; preparing it from cash book or pass book balances or extracts; preparing an amended cash book.

chapters.name: Depreciation
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (10 marks): the meaning and causes of depreciation; Straight Line and Written Down Value methods; recording through the asset account or a provision for depreciation; purchase and sale of assets.

chapters.name: Bills of Exchange
chapters.summary: Unit 6 (7 marks): negotiable instruments, bills of exchange, promissory notes and cheques, and related terms; entries for endorsement, discounting, dishonour, renewal and retirement in the books of the drawer, drawee and endorsee.

chapters.name: Final Accounts
chapters.summary: Unit 7 (14 marks): capital and revenue items; provisions and reserves; the Trading and Profit and Loss Account and Balance Sheet of a sole trader, with and without adjustments; marshalling of the Balance Sheet.

chapters.name: Rectification of Errors
chapters.summary: Unit 8 (8 marks): errors of omission, commission and principle, and compensating errors; rectifying errors after the Trial Balance and after the Final Accounts; the Suspense Account.

chapters.name: Accounting for Not-for-Profit Organisations
chapters.summary: Unit 9 (10 marks): the Receipts and Payments Account, the Income and Expenditure Account and the Balance Sheet; preparing Income and Expenditure accounts from Receipts and Payments data; treating special items.

chapters.name: Computerised Accounting System (CAS)
chapters.summary: Unit 10 (3 marks): the components, features, advantages and limitations of CAS, and the Accounting Information System.

commerce.overview: In the ISC 2027 syllabus (the latest that lists Commerce; the ISC 2028 syllabus page has no Commerce document), Class XI Commerce is an 80-mark, three-hour theory paper of eight units plus 20 marks of project work.

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2027 - Commerce (857), CISCE, February 2025
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1: unit weightage table); PDF pp. 5-7 (printed pp. 2-4: Paper I units 1-8)

chapters.name: Nature and Purpose of Business
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (10 marks): economic and non-economic activities; how business, profession and employment differ; industry (by activity and size) and commerce (trade and aids to trade); business objectives and the role of profit.

chapters.name: Forms of Business Organisation
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (25 marks): private, public and joint sectors and PPPs; sole trader; partnership (deed, registration, types of partners); joint stock companies (formation, promotion, incorporation, MOA and AOA, prospectus, public and private companies, global enterprises); public sector undertakings; co-operatives.

chapters.name: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (5 marks): the concept of and need for social responsibility towards owners, investors, consumers, employees, government, the community and the environment; the meaning and importance of business ethics.

chapters.name: Emerging Modes of Business
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (5 marks): e-business (scope, resources, online transactions, payment, security); e-commerce; quick commerce and the use of artificial intelligence, including dark stores.

chapters.name: Stock Exchange
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (5 marks): the meaning, functions and services of a stock exchange; BSE and NSE; brokers, jobbers, bulls and bears; terms such as ex-dividend and cum-dividend; SEBI; the demat account.

chapters.name: Trade
chapters.summary: Unit 6 (10 marks): the services of wholesalers; retail trade and its types (itinerant, fixed shops, departmental and chain stores, vending machines); documents in home trade; trade and cash discounts.

chapters.name: Foreign Trade
chapters.summary: Unit 7 (10 marks): internal versus international trade; export and import procedures; documents in export and import trade; the WTO.

chapters.name: Insurance
chapters.summary: Unit 8 (10 marks): the meaning of insurance, re-insurance and double insurance; insurable and non-insurable risks; the principles of insurance; types of insurance (life, health, fire, marine, motor, social, fidelity).

economics.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Economics is an 80-mark, three-hour theory paper in three units (Understanding Economics, Indian Economic Development, Statistics), plus 20 marks of project work (two projects).

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Economics (856), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF pp. 4-6 (printed pp. 1-3: Class XI Paper I units 1-3)

chapters.name: Definitions of Economics
chapters.summary: Unit 1(i): the definitions of economics given by Adam Smith, Alfred Marshall, Lionel Robbins and Samuelson, their features and criticisms, framed by scarcity and the allocation of resources.

chapters.name: Micro and Macro Economics and Basic Concepts
chapters.summary: Unit 1(ii): micro versus macro economics; basic concepts - wants, factors of production, utility (total, marginal, diminishing), price, value, wealth, welfare, money, market, capital, investment, income, production, consumption and saving.

chapters.name: Basic Problems of an Economy
chapters.summary: Unit 1(iii): what, how and for whom to produce; scarcity and choice explained with the Production Possibility Curve, including shifts and rotation due to technology.

chapters.name: Types of Economies and Economic Systems
chapters.summary: Unit 1(iv): developed and developing economies; regional and global groupings (SAARC, EU, ASEAN, G-8, G-20); capitalism, socialism and the mixed economy, and how each solves the basic problems through the price mechanism and government.

chapters.name: Indian Economy Post Liberalisation
chapters.summary: Unit 2(i): the main features, problems and policies of agriculture, industry and foreign trade in India after liberalisation.

chapters.name: Parameters of Development
chapters.summary: Unit 2(ii): per capita income and its limitations; the meaning and construction of the Human Development Index; India's position in the UNDP report.

chapters.name: Planning and Economic Development in India
chapters.summary: Unit 2(iii): the objectives of the Five-Year Plans; NITI Aayog's objectives and role.

chapters.name: Structural Changes in the Indian Economy after Liberalisation
chapters.summary: Unit 2(iv): the need for, meaning and features of liberalisation, globalisation and privatisation; the meaning of disinvestment.

chapters.name: Current Challenges Facing the Indian Economy
chapters.summary: Unit 2(v): poverty and poverty-alleviation programmes; rural credit, agricultural marketing, cooperatives and organic farming; human capital formation and education; types, causes and policy measures for unemployment.

chapters.name: Economic Growth and Development
chapters.summary: Unit 2(vi): the meaning of economic growth and development and how they differ.

chapters.name: Sustainable Development
chapters.summary: Unit 2(vii): the effect of development on resources and the environment; the concept of and need for sustainable development; global warming.

chapters.name: Statistics: Definition, Scope and Limitations
chapters.summary: Unit 3(i): the definition, scope and limitations of statistics and its importance in economics.

chapters.name: Collection, Organisation and Presentation of Data
chapters.summary: Unit 3(ii): primary and secondary data and how they are collected; variables and frequency; tables, bar and pie diagrams, line graphs, histograms, polygons and ogives.

chapters.name: Measures of Central Value
chapters.summary: Unit 3(iii): simple and weighted arithmetic mean, median and mode for ungrouped and grouped data; the relationship between mean, median and mode; symmetrical and skewed distributions.

chapters.name: Measures of Dispersion
chapters.summary: Unit 3(iv): range, quartile deviation, mean deviation, standard deviation and coefficient of variation, with numericals.

chapters.name: Correlation
chapters.summary: Unit 3(v): the meaning, types and degrees of correlation; scatter diagrams; Karl Pearson's coefficient and Spearman's rank correlation.

chapters.name: Index Numbers
chapters.summary: Unit 3(vi): simple and weighted index numbers; the Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher methods; WPI, CPI and the Index of Industrial Production; uses of index numbers and problems in constructing a price index.

chapters.name: Some Mathematical Tools Used in Economics
chapters.summary: Unit 3(vii): the equation and slope of a straight line.

computer-science.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Computer Science is a 70-mark, three-hour theory paper in three sections (A: Hardware, B: Java, C: Python and conceptual aspects), plus a 30-mark practical paper in Java.

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Computer Science (868), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 2: unit and marks table); PDF pp. 6-9 (printed pp. 3-6: Paper I units 1-13)

chapters.name: System of Numeration
chapters.summary: Section A, Unit 1: numbers in binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal and converting between them; addition, subtraction (1's and 2's complement) and multiplication in different bases.

chapters.name: Encodings
chapters.summary: Section A, Unit 2: character encodings (ASCII, ISCII, Unicode) and the limits of ASCII for other languages.

chapters.name: Propositional Logic, Hardware Implementation, Arithmetic Operations
chapters.summary: Section A, Unit 3: logical connectives, well-formed formulae, truth tables, and satisfiable, unsatisfiable and valid formulae; basic and universal gates, NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR; half and full adders.

chapters.name: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming using Java
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 4: an introduction to object-oriented programming in Java, taught alongside units 5-11 together with classes and their definitions.

chapters.name: Objects
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 5: objects as attributes plus behaviour, and objects versus classes; real-world examples; the JVM, javac and java; compile-time and run-time errors; exceptions with try-catch, throw, throws and finally.

chapters.name: Primitive Values, Wrapper Classes, Types and Casting
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 6: primitive types and their wrapper classes; classes as user-defined types; casting and automatic type coercion.

chapters.name: Variables, Expressions
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 7: variables and named constants (final); arithmetic and logical expressions and their evaluation, with precedence and associativity; assignment; primitive versus reference variables.

chapters.name: Statements, Scope
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 8: conditional statements (if, if-else, switch-case, the ternary operator); loops (for, while, do-while) with break and continue; blocks; block, method and class scope and visibility.

chapters.name: Methods and Constructors
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 9: formal and actual arguments; side effects; static methods and variables; the this operator; constructors and the new operator; problem solving with methods.

chapters.name: Arrays, Strings
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 10: single- and multi-dimensional arrays; searching and bubble, selection and insertion sorts; String class operations (characters, substrings, concatenation, replacement, indexOf).

chapters.name: Basic Input/Output and Text File Handling
chapters.summary: Section B, Unit 11: input with the Scanner class; tokens, delimiters and StringTokenizer; I/O exceptions; data file handling with FileReader and FileWriter (create, read, write, append, search).

chapters.name: Introduction to Python
chapters.summary: Section C, Unit 12: installing Python and IDEs; Python fundamentals, tokens and variables; data types (numbers, boolean, string, list, tuple, None, dictionary); input and output and errors; operators and type conversion; conditional and iterative flow of control.

chapters.name: Trends in Computing and Ethical Issues
chapters.summary: Section C, Unit 13: AI, IoT, VR and AR; cyber security, privacy, netiquette, spam, phishing and digital arrest; intellectual property, software copyright, patents and licensing (GPL, BSD), and the Free Software Foundation.

business-studies.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Business Studies is an 80-mark, three-hour theory paper of five units, from Business: Purpose and Classification to Business Risks and Insurance, plus 20 marks of project work (two projects).

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Business Studies (857), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1: unit weightage table); PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 2-3: Paper I units 1-5)

chapters.name: Business: Purpose and Classification
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (10 marks): the meaning and features of business; economic and social objectives and the role of profit; industry (primary, secondary, tertiary; micro to large) and commerce (trade and aids to trade); business ethics and CSR (meaning only).

chapters.name: Forms and Types of Business Organisations
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (30 marks): private and public sectors and PPPs; sole proprietorship; partnership (deed, registration, types of partners and firms, LLP); joint stock companies (formation, promotion, incorporation, MOA and AOA, commencement, prospectus, global enterprises); co-operatives and multistate co-operative societies.

chapters.name: Contemporary and Evolving Modes of Business
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (15 marks): e-business (payments, blockchain, crypto-assets, security); e-commerce, quick commerce and artificial intelligence; e-banking (RTGS, NEFT, IMPS, UPI, e-wallets, the digital rupee), mobile banking, debit and credit cards, online demand drafts.

chapters.name: Domestic Trade
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (10 marks): wholesale trade and the services of wholesalers; retail trade and its types (itinerant, fixed shops, departmental, chain and dark stores); digital and omnichannel retailing.

chapters.name: Business Risks and Insurance
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (15 marks): insurable and non-insurable risks; the meaning and principles of insurance; re-insurance and double insurance; assurance versus insurance; types of insurance.

artificial-intelligence.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Artificial Intelligence is a 70-mark, three-hour theory paper of seven units, plus a 30-mark practical component made up of a practical examination, project work and a practical file.

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Artificial Intelligence (883), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1: unit weightage table); PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 2-3: Paper I units 1-7)

chapters.name: Basic Concepts of Artificial Intelligence
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (8 marks): the definition, evolution, applications and benefits of AI; data types and exploring data, binary logic and gates, deterministic and probabilistic problems; decision making in machines and cyber security; the AI project framework; data representation and programming in Python.

chapters.name: Introduction and State of Art of AI, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Potential Use of AI
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (8 marks): machine learning, deep learning and neural networks and their applications; the NLP domain (text understanding and generation, translation, chatbots, voice assistants, types of search); uses of AI in various domains; AI and society.

chapters.name: Mathematics for AI
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (12 marks): matrices and matrix operations; vectors; set theory, relational algebra and data table joins; mean, median, mode, variance and standard deviation.

chapters.name: Data Visualization
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (16 marks): visualisation with matplotlib, seaborn and Excel; handling missing values and outliers with pandas; bar graphs, histograms, scatter plots and pie charts; the dimensionality of data.

chapters.name: Theoretical and Practical Aspects of Data Processing
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (8 marks): data cleaning with pandas; exploring Kaggle datasets with DataFrames; transforming and standardising data.

chapters.name: Data Modelling, Simple Linear Regression
chapters.summary: Unit 6 (12 marks): dimensional, relational and entity-relational data models; regression analysis; the least-squares regression line and regression coefficient; solving linear equations.

chapters.name: Ethical Practices in AI
chapters.summary: Unit 7 (6 marks): an AI code of ethics - avoiding bias, protecting user privacy and data, reducing environmental impact - and why AI ethics matters.

environmental-science.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Environmental Science is a 70-mark, three-hour theory paper of seven units, plus 30 marks of project work (two projects).

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Environmental Science (877), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1: unit weightage table); PDF pp. 5-10 (printed pp. 2-7: Paper I units 1-7)

chapters.name: Environment - The Foundation of Life
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (5 marks): why Environmental Science is studied, and its scope and applications.

chapters.name: Modes of Existence
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (7 marks): hunting-gathering, pastoral, agricultural and industrial modes of existence; their use of resources, ecological impact, social organisation and view of the relationship between people and nature (case studies of the Sentinelese and the Jarawa); how the modes coexist in India and the conflicts between them.

chapters.name: Ecology
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (15 marks): ecosystems, food chains and webs, and relationships between organisms; habitats, niches and competitive exclusion; energy flow and ecological pyramids; nutrient cycles and ecological succession; terrestrial, freshwater and marine biomes.

chapters.name: Pollution
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (15 marks): air pollution, the greenhouse effect and ozone depletion; pollution prevention and control (Pollution Control Boards, catalytic converters, scrubbers, precipitators); indoor pollution; water, soil, radioactive, noise and microplastic pollution; coastal zone management.

chapters.name: Legal Regimes for Sustainable Development
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (10 marks): constitutional provisions and Indian environmental laws (the Environment Protection, Forest Conservation, Wildlife Protection, Biological Diversity, Water and Air Acts); the National Environment Policy; the NGT and its landmark cases; international regimes and institutions (UNEP, UNCTAD, WHO, UNDP, the Earth Summit, Agenda 21).

chapters.name: Technology and Environment
chapters.summary: Unit 6 (10 marks): hi-tech, low-tech, intermediate, appropriate and traditional technology; Green AI; renewable energy sources; disease as an indicator of environmental health, sanitation and health services; traditional medicine and AYUSH; the potential and limits of biotechnology; bioremediation.

chapters.name: Design and Planning for Environmental Conservation and Protection
chapters.summary: Unit 7 (8 marks): ecosystem analysis (critical and state variables, indicator species, resilience); interactions between people and the environment and analysing issues through a case study; designing solutions in line with EIA, with the Goa beach tourism case study and a second case study of environmental sustainability.

biotechnology.overview: In the ISC 2028 syllabus, Class XI Biotechnology is a 70-mark, three-hour theory paper of five units, plus a 30-mark practical component made up of practical work, project work and a practical file.

syllabusSource.title: ISC Examination Year 2028 - Biotechnology (878), CISCE
syllabusSource.pages: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1: unit weightage table); PDF pp. 5-7 (printed pp. 2-4: Paper I units 1-5)

chapters.name: Introduction to Biotechnology
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (12 marks): the history and definitions (OECD, EFB) of biotechnology and key contributors; fermentation (curd, lactic acid, alcohol, beer); GLP and GMP; branches of biotechnology, IPR, ethical, legal and social issues (ELSI), biosafety and GEAC; Indian and global institutes; acids and bases, pH, buffers, probability and data types.

chapters.name: Cell Biology
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (14 marks): prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; bacterial cell structure and Gram staining; cell organelles; chromosome organisation; the cell cycle and its regulation, mitosis and meiosis, mitotic index; stem cells; signal transduction; apoptosis; microscopy and karyotyping.

chapters.name: Biomolecules, Techniques to Separate the Biomolecules and Defence Strategies in Organisms
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (17 marks): carbohydrates, proteins and amino acids, lipids, vitamins and enzymes (mechanism, kinetics, inhibition); ion exchange and paper chromatography, centrifugation and isoelectric focusing; the immune system, ELISA, HLA and MHC; defence strategies and secondary metabolites in plants.

chapters.name: Genetics
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (12 marks): Mendel's experiments and laws; trait, gene, allele, genotype and phenotype; mutations and chromosomal aberrations; Turner's, Klinefelter's and Down's syndromes; inborn errors of metabolism; linkage, crossover value and gene mapping; cancer genetics.

chapters.name: Introduction to Cell Culture Technology
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (15 marks): cell culture instruments (LAF, autoclave, haemocytometer, incubator and others); sterilisation; FACS sorting, cell counting and viability testing; nutrient media (LB, MS, White's, RPMI, DMEM, FBS) and their preparation; cryopreservation.

physics.overview: ISC Class XII Physics has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory is organised into nine units from Electrostatics to Electronic Devices. The units' numbered sub-units match the rationalised NCERT chapter titles and are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 syllabus: Physics, Class XII

chapters.name: Electric Charges and Fields
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Electrostatics (i). Coulomb's law, electric field and dipole, lines of force, and Gauss's theorem.

chapters.name: Electrostatic Potential, Potential Energy and Capacitance
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Electrostatics (ii). Potential and potential energy, capacitors and dielectrics.

chapters.name: Current Electricity
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Current Electricity. Drift velocity and mobility, Ohm's law, emf, Kirchhoff's laws, and electrical energy and billing.

chapters.name: Moving Charges and Magnetism
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism (i). Oersted's experiment, the Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, and forces on charges and conductors.

chapters.name: Magnetism and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism (ii). The current loop as a magnetic dipole, and magnetic properties of materials.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Induction
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents (i).

chapters.name: Alternating Current
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents (ii). RMS values, reactance, LCR circuits (phasors) and resonance.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Waves
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Electromagnetic Waves. Displacement current, properties of EM waves, and the electromagnetic spectrum.

chapters.name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
chapters.summary: Unit 6: Optics (i). Reflection, refraction, prisms, lenses and optical instruments.

chapters.name: Wave Optics
chapters.summary: Unit 6: Optics (ii). Wavefronts, Huygens' principle, interference (Young's double slit) and diffraction.

chapters.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit 7: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter. The photoelectric effect, Einstein's equation, and de Broglie waves (Davisson-Germer, qualitative).

chapters.name: Atoms
chapters.summary: Unit 8: Atoms and Nuclei (i). Rutherford's model, Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, and spectral series.

chapters.name: Nuclei
chapters.summary: Unit 8: Atoms and Nuclei (ii). Composition and size of the nucleus, mass-energy relation, binding energy, fission and fusion.

chapters.name: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
chapters.summary: Unit 9: Electronic Devices (i) and (ii). Energy bands, p-n junction, diode as a rectifier, LED, photodiode, solar cell and the Zener diode as a voltage regulator.

chemistry.overview: ISC Class XII Chemistry has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory has 10 units weighted by branch: Physical Chemistry (units 1–3) 25 marks, Inorganic Chemistry (units 4–5) 14 marks and Organic Chemistry (units 6–10) 31 marks.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 syllabus: Chemistry, Class XII

chapters.name: Solutions
chapters.summary: Physical Chemistry, Unit 1. Concentration, Raoult's law, colligative properties, abnormal molecular mass and the van't Hoff factor.

chapters.name: Electrochemistry
chapters.summary: Physical Chemistry, Unit 2. Electrode potentials, the Nernst equation, conductance and electrolysis.

mathematics.overview: ISC Class XII Mathematics (860) has a 3-hour, 80-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 20-mark project (Paper II). The ISC 2027 syllabus is NOT divided into Sections A/B/C. It lists seven units: Relations and Functions (10 marks), Algebra (10), Calculus (35), Vector Algebra (5), Three-Dimensional Geometry (6), Linear Programming (5) and Probability (9). science.overview: CBSE Class 10 Science (subject code 086) follows the NCERT textbook and covers chemistry (reactions, acids and bases, metals, carbon compounds), biology (life processes, control and coordination, reproduction, heredity, environment) and physics (light, the human eye, electricity and magnetism). The board paper is 80 marks in 3 hours, with 20 marks of internal assessment.
studyTips: Work through the official CBSE question papers and marking schemes for recent years: the marking scheme shows the value points examiners look for.
Practise balanced chemical equations and ray diagrams until you can draw them without looking.
For case-based questions, read the passage first and underline the data each sub-part refers to.
Revise definitions and laws word for word; short answers are marked against specific value points.

chapters.summary: The nervous system, reflex actions and the human brain, coordination in plants through plant hormones, and hormones in animals.

chapters.summary: Modes of asexual reproduction, sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans, and reproductive health.

studyTips: Solve the official CBSE question papers for recent years under timed conditions, then compare your working with the marking scheme.
Write every step: the marking scheme awards marks for method as well as the final answer.

physics.overview: CBSE Class 12 Physics (code 042) has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper across 9 units and 14 NCERT chapters, plus 30 marks of practicals. The units run from Electrostatics to Electronic Devices and follow the rationalised NCERT Class XII Physics Parts I and II.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Physics (Code 042), Class XII

chapters.name: Electric Charges and Fields
chapters.summary: Unit I: Electrostatics. Coulomb's law, electric field and dipoles, electric flux and Gauss's theorem.

chapters.name: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
chapters.summary: Unit I: Electrostatics. Potential, equipotential surfaces, potential energy, dielectrics and capacitors.

chapters.name: Current Electricity
chapters.summary: Unit II: Current Electricity. Drift velocity, Ohm's law, resistivity, emf and internal resistance, Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge.

chapters.name: Moving Charges and Magnetism
chapters.summary: Unit III: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism. Biot-Savart and Ampere's laws, forces on moving charges and currents, and the moving coil galvanometer.

chapters.name: Magnetism and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit III: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism. The bar magnet as a magnetic dipole, field lines, and para-, dia- and ferromagnetic materials.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Induction
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents. Faraday's laws, Lenz's law, and self and mutual induction.

chapters.name: Alternating Current
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents. RMS values, reactance and impedance, LCR circuits, resonance, power factor, AC generator and transformer.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Waves
chapters.summary: Unit V: Electromagnetic Waves. Displacement current, characteristics of EM waves, and the electromagnetic spectrum.

chapters.name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Optics. Reflection, refraction, total internal reflection, lenses, prisms, microscopes and telescopes.

chapters.name: Wave Optics
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Optics. Huygens' principle, interference and Young's double slit, and single-slit diffraction.

chapters.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter. The photoelectric effect, Einstein's equation and de Broglie matter waves.

chapters.name: Atoms
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Atoms and Nuclei. Alpha-particle scattering, Rutherford's model, and the Bohr model and line spectra of hydrogen.

chapters.name: Nuclei
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Atoms and Nuclei. Nuclear composition and size, mass defect, binding energy, fission and fusion.

chapters.name: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
chapters.summary: Unit IX: Electronic Devices. Energy bands, intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, the p-n junction, and the diode as a rectifier.

chemistry.overview: CBSE Class 12 Chemistry (code 043) has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper over 10 units, plus 30 marks of practicals. The syllabus covers physical chemistry (solutions, electrochemistry, kinetics), inorganic chemistry (d- and f-block elements, coordination compounds) and organic chemistry (haloalkanes to biomolecules). It is based on the NCERT Class XII Chemistry Parts I and II.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Chemistry (Code 043), Class XII

chapters.name: Solutions
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (7 marks). Concentration, Raoult's law, colligative properties and the van't Hoff factor.

chapters.name: Electrochemistry
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (9 marks). EMF, the Nernst equation, conductance, Kohlrausch's law, batteries, fuel cells and corrosion.

chapters.name: Chemical Kinetics
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (7 marks). Rate laws, order and molecularity, integrated rate equations, half-life and the Arrhenius equation.

chapters.name: d- and f-Block Elements
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (7 marks). Trends in transition metals, K2Cr2O7 and KMnO4, lanthanides and actinides.

chapters.name: Coordination Compounds
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (7 marks). Ligands, IUPAC nomenclature, Werner's theory, VBT and CFT, and isomerism.

chapters.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
chapters.summary: Unit 6 (6 marks). The C–X bond, substitution mechanisms, and uses and environmental effects of polyhalogen compounds.

chapters.name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
chapters.summary: Unit 7 (6 marks). Preparation, properties and uses of alcohols, phenols and ethers.

chapters.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
chapters.summary: Unit 8 (8 marks). The carbonyl group, nucleophilic addition, alpha-hydrogen reactivity, and carboxylic acids.

chapters.name: Amines
chapters.summary: Unit 9 (6 marks). Classification, preparation and properties of amines, and diazonium salts.

chapters.name: Biomolecules
chapters.summary: Unit 10 (7 marks). Carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins and nucleic acids.

biology.overview: CBSE Class 12 Biology (code 044) has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper across five units (VI–X) and 13 chapters, plus 30 marks of practicals. The units are Reproduction (16 marks), Genetics and Evolution (20), Biology and Human Welfare (12), Biotechnology and its Applications (12), and Ecology and Environment (10).

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Biology (Code 044), Class XII

chapters.name: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Reproduction. Flower structure, gametophytes, pollination, double fertilisation, seed and fruit formation.

chapters.name: Human Reproduction
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Reproduction. Reproductive systems, gametogenesis, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation, implantation and pregnancy.

chapters.name: Reproductive Health
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Reproduction. STD prevention, contraception, MTP, amniocentesis, infertility and ART.

chapters.name: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Genetics and Evolution. Mendelian inheritance and deviations, sex determination, linkage, and genetic disorders.

chapters.name: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Genetics and Evolution. DNA structure and replication, the central dogma, the lac operon, genome projects and DNA fingerprinting.

chapters.name: Evolution
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Genetics and Evolution. The origin of life, evidences and mechanisms of evolution, Hardy-Weinberg principle and human evolution.

chapters.name: Human Health and Diseases
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Biology and Human Welfare. Pathogens and diseases, immunology and vaccines, cancer, HIV/AIDS, and drug and alcohol abuse.

chapters.name: Microbes in Human Welfare
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Biology and Human Welfare. Microbes in food, industry, sewage treatment, energy, biocontrol and biofertilisers.

chapters.name: Biotechnology - Principles and Processes
chapters.summary: Unit IX: Biotechnology and its Applications. Genetic engineering (recombinant DNA technology).

chapters.name: Biotechnology and its Applications
chapters.summary: Unit IX: Biotechnology and its Applications. Insulin and vaccine production, gene therapy, Bt crops, transgenic animals and biosafety.

chapters.name: Organisms and Populations
chapters.summary: Unit X: Ecology and Environment. Population interactions and population attributes.

chapters.name: Ecosystem
chapters.summary: Unit X: Ecology and Environment. Ecosystem components, productivity, decomposition, energy flow and ecological pyramids.

chapters.name: Biodiversity and its Conservation
chapters.summary: Unit X: Ecology and Environment. Patterns and loss of biodiversity, hotspots and in-situ/ex-situ conservation.

mathematics.overview: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics (code 041) has one 80-mark theory paper and 20 marks of internal assessment. The paper covers six units: Relations and Functions (8 marks), Algebra (10), Calculus (35), Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry (14), Linear Programming (5) and Probability (8). These units contain 13 NCERT chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Mathematics (Code 041), Class XII

chapters.name: Relations and Functions
chapters.summary: Unit I: Relations and Functions. Types of relations, equivalence relations, and one-one and onto functions.

chapters.name: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
chapters.summary: Unit I: Relations and Functions. Domain, range, principal value branches and graphs.

chapters.name: Matrices
chapters.summary: Unit II: Algebra. Types of matrices, matrix operations, transpose, symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices, and invertibility.

chapters.name: Determinants
chapters.summary: Unit II: Algebra. Determinants up to 3 × 3, minors and cofactors, adjoint and inverse, and solving linear systems.

chapters.name: Continuity and Differentiability
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. The chain rule, implicit and parametric differentiation, logarithmic differentiation and second-order derivatives.

chapters.name: Applications of Derivatives
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Rate of change, increasing and decreasing functions, and maxima and minima.

chapters.name: Integrals
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Integration by substitution, partial fractions and parts, and definite integrals and their properties.

chapters.name: Application of the Integrals
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Area under simple curves (lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses in standard form).

chapters.name: Differential Equations
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Order and degree, separation of variables, and homogeneous and linear first-order equations.

chapters.name: Vectors
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry. Types of vectors, components, section formula, and dot and cross products.

chapters.name: Three-dimensional Geometry
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry. Direction cosines and ratios, equations of a line, skew lines and shortest distance.

chapters.name: Linear Programming
chapters.summary: Unit V: Linear Programming Problem. Graphical solution of two-variable problems with up to three non-trivial constraints.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Probability. Conditional probability, the multiplication theorem, independent events, total probability and Bayes' theorem.
